column7: Increase climate resilience and competitiveness of the agriculture sector
column12: The Project Development Objective is to increase climate resilience and competitiveness of the agriculture sector.

column7: Develop farm and client registers, upgraded payment system and Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN)
column12: The subcomponent will support establishing farm and client registers, upgrading the payment system, strengthening the Country Agriculture Rural Payment Office, and establishing a Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN).

column7: Support climate-resilient agriculture through improved seeds, climate risk awareness, extension services, and diversification strategies
column12: The project will raise awareness on climate change impacts, improve extension services, promote adoption of Good Agricultural Practices and integrated pest management, facilitate climate risk assessment, and support diversification strategies such as agroforestry and intercropping using improved seeds.

column7: Provide matching grants and capacity building to aggregators for climate-smart value-chain investments across fruits, vegetables, dairy and livestock
column12: The project will strengthen value chains by providing matching grants to aggregators for investments in renewable energy, cold chain, climate-smart post-harvest storage and processing across fruits, vegetables, dairy and livestock; technical assistance and capacity building will accompany these investments.
column17: Component 2 (Strengthening value chains and productive partnerships)

column7: Rehabilitate irrigation and drainage systems and develop new energy-efficient schemes with training for water user associations
column12: Subcomponent 2 will rehabilitate irrigation networks, promote energy-efficient irrigation and renewable energy, develop new irrigation schemes and provide capacity building for water user associations, including operations and maintenance agreements and an Irrigation and Drainage Information Management System.

column7: Upgrade food quality and safety institutions and laboratories to meet EU standards
column12: The project will invest in food quality and safety by upgrading laboratories and risk-based controls, strengthening veterinary, food safety and plant health institutions, conducting risk assessments and ensuring compliance with EU food safety standards.

column7: Develop integrated IT systems for veterinary, food safety and plant health information and traceability
column12: An IT system will be developed to integrate veterinary, food safety and plant health information for real-time traceability and ensure compatibility with EU systems, strengthening official controls and documentation.

column7: Farmers adopting improved agricultural technology
column12: The results framework includes an indicator for the number of farmers adopting improved agricultural technology, disaggregated by gender, reflecting adoption of climate-smart production practices and technologies.

column7: Farmers with access to irrigation or drainage services supported by the project
column12: The PDO indicator “Farmers with access to irrigation/drainage services supported by the project” measures the area and number of farmers served by rehabilitated or new irrigation schemes, aiming to enhance climate resilience.

column7: Aggregators reporting increased sales of agricultural produce
column12: One of the PDO indicators tracks the percentage of aggregators reporting increases in sales of agricultural produce from farmers they support, reflecting improved market efficiency and commercialization.

column7: Increase in percentage of risk‑based official controls in veterinary, food safety and plant health services
column12: The project aims to increase the percentage of improved risk‑based official controls by veterinary, food safety and plant health services, enhancing institutional capacity and regulatory compliance.

column7: Farm and client registry improved and new value‑chain registers established
column12: Intermediate indicators include improvement of the farm and client registry and establishment of new registers for priority value chains to enhance targeting and transparency of support programs.

column7: Establishment of a Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN)
column12: The results framework includes an intermediate indicator for establishing a Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN), contributing to transparent and evidence-based agricultural policy.

column7: Extension staff trained in climate‑smart production practices and number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services
column12: Intermediate indicators track the number of extension staff trained in climate‑smart production practices, including women, as well as the number of farmers (male and female) reached with agricultural assets or services, reflecting efforts to build capacity and inclusivity.

column7: Area provided with new or improved irrigation or drainage services
column12: An intermediate indicator measures the hectares of area provided with new or improved irrigation or drainage services, highlighting investment in climate‑resilient infrastructure.

column7: Number of upgraded veterinary and food safety laboratories and adoption of IT systems
column12: Intermediate indicators measure the number of veterinary and food safety laboratories upgraded and the adoption of new IT systems by staff (with female disaggregation), reflecting strengthening of regulatory and control capacity.

Enhance productivity and commercialization of non‑pastoral animal production and strengthen capacity to respond to crises
column12: The project development objectives are to enhance productivity and commercialization of non‑pastoral animal production in selected value chains and strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to severe crises affecting the livestock sector, providing immediate and effective response in an eligible emergency.

column7: Improve access to animal health services through vaccination campaigns, disease surveillance and laboratory rehabilitation
column12: Subcomponent 1.1 finances vaccination campaigns against priority diseases such as CBPP, FMD, fowl pox, PPR, ASF and HPAI, strengthens disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity, rehabilitates veterinary laboratories and posts, and trains veterinary services to improve animal health.

column7: Improve access to quality inputs including feed, forage seeds and superior genetics through artificial insemination and improved fingerlings
column11: cattle; dairy; small ruminants; poultry; swine; fish
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 improves access to quality inputs by supporting feed quality control, producing forage seeds, providing high‑performance bulls for genetic improvement, expanding artificial insemination, regulating animal genetic resources and introducing improved fingerlings for aquaculture.

column7: Strengthen institutions through training, guidelines, rehabilitation of veterinary posts and markets and central procurement of veterinary drugs
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 provides institutional strengthening by developing technical guidelines, transferring new farming techniques, training veterinary school staff (with emphasis on women), rehabilitating veterinary posts and markets, raising awareness about quality standards and establishing a central procurement unit to combat counterfeit veterinary medicines.

column7: Enhance the investment climate through studies, training and capacity building for financial institutions and private sector actors
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 finances studies, training, business exchanges and strategic planning to improve the investment climate, promotes livestock product branding and quality certification and builds capacity of partner financial institutions to develop tailored financial products for livestock investors.

column7: Provide matching grants to productive alliances and micro‑projects for equipment, livestock and inputs with favourable terms for women and youth
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 provides matching grants to productive alliances and micro‑projects to finance equipment, small civil works, live animals and inputs. Grants include capacity building and more favourable terms for women and youth to support inclusive value‑chain development.

column7: Strengthen crisis management through operationalizing the Permanent Secretariat, developing crisis tools and contingency responses
column12: Component 3 supports crisis management by operationalizing the Permanent Secretariat for livestock crises, providing equipment, training and tools for crisis management and establishing a Contingency Emergency Response mechanism to respond rapidly to livestock shocks.

column7: Increase in yields of selected animal value chains
column11: cattle; dairy; small ruminants; poultry; swine
column12: PDO indicators include a percentage increase in yields for selected animal value chains (targeting a 20 percent gain), reflecting improved productivity in cattle, small ruminant, milk, poultry and pork value chains.

column7: Incremental sales in targeted value chains
column11: cattle; dairy; small ruminants; poultry; swine
column12: A PDO indicator measures incremental sales in targeted value chains (target 30 percent), indicating enhanced commercialization and market efficiency for livestock producers.

column7: Reduced prevalence of animal diseases such as CBPP and PPR
column12: Intermediate results indicators track reductions in prevalence of Contagious Bovine Pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) as a result of improved vaccination and disease surveillance.

column7: Number of poultry vaccinated against priority diseases
column12: The results framework counts the number of poultry vaccinated against diseases like fowl pox and highly pathogenic avian influenza, showing efforts to control epidemics and increase resilience.

column7: Farmers adopting improved agricultural technology
column12: An intermediate indicator records the number of farmers adopting improved agricultural technology, such as better feeding practices or animal management methods, indicating diffusion of innovations.

column7: Farmers reached with agricultural assets or services (male, female, youth)
column12: PDO and intermediate indicators track the number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services, including disaggregation by female and youth beneficiaries, reflecting inclusive outreach and adoption of technologies.

column7: Number of micro‑projects funded and volume of loans granted by partner financial institutions
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of micro-projects funded (with female and youth disaggregation) and the volume of loans granted by partner financial institutions, supporting diversification and access to finance.

column7: Time between crisis requests and disbursement and beneficiary satisfaction rate
column12: Indicators measure the number of weeks between a crisis request and disbursement under the Contingency Emergency Response and the beneficiary satisfaction rate with services, reflecting responsiveness and resilience capacity.

column7: Improve productivity, commercialization and resilience of key sedentary livestock production systems for targeted beneficiaries
column12: The Project Development Objective is to improve the productivity, commercialization and resilience of key sedentary livestock production systems for targeted beneficiaries in project areas.

column7: Develop Livestock Master Plan, update feeding, breeding, dairy and animal health policies and improve food safety and SPS regulations
column12: Subcomponent 1.1 provides technical assistance to prepare a Livestock Master Plan, update policies on feeding, breeding, dairy and animal health, improve food safety and SPS regulations, develop a genetic resource management strategy and build the Ministry’s capacity for climate‑smart policy formulation and M&E.

column7: Strengthen animal husbandry and advisory services through GAHP training, extension support, improved breeds and drought‑tolerant forage seeds
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 supports animal husbandry by developing training materials and farmer field schools, training extension agents, distributing improved bulls and establishing artificial insemination centres, providing drought‑tolerant forage seeds, and supplying livestock to internally displaced and conflict‑affected populations.

column7: Enhance animal health services through disease surveillance, training and vaccination programs for CBPP, FMD, Newcastle disease, Fowl Pox and PPR
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 strengthens animal health services by improving surveillance and control of endemic and emerging diseases, rehabilitating quarantine posts, training farmers and veterinarians, and delivering vaccination campaigns targeting diseases such as CBPP, FMD, Newcastle disease, Fowl Pox and PPR. It also provides vaccines, solar‑powered cold chains, strengthens laboratories, digitalizes livestock identification, supports One Health implementation and equips private veterinary practitioners.

column7: Develop climate‑smart productive infrastructure and markets including cooling centres, transport, slaughterhouses, climate‑smart markets and food safety laboratories
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 finances climate‑resilient livestock infrastructure such as cooling centres, transport services, slaughterhouses and climate‑smart livestock markets with water, shade and weighbridges. It upgrades abattoirs, links producers and traders, improves price discovery, professionalizes trade, upgrades the ABNORM food certification laboratory and develops an integrated Livestock Market Information System (LMIS).

column7: Improve access to finance through business development services, capacity building for PFIs and establishment of the Livestock Improvement Financial Facility
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 provides business development services to livestock value‑chain actors, builds capacity of partner financial institutions, and establishes a Livestock Improvement Financial Facility to provide matching grants for climate‑smart productive investments, with carbon impact assessments and prioritization of women and youth.

column7: Increase in productivity of livestock species (milk yield and carcass weight)
column12: PDO indicators measure increases in productivity of key livestock species, such as higher milk yield per cow and heavier carcass weights for cattle, sheep and goats, reflecting improved feeding and husbandry practices.

column7: Increase in volume of market sales for milk, meat and eggs
column12: The results framework tracks increases in the volume of sales of milk, meat and eggs by producers supported by the project, indicating enhanced commercialization and market linkages.

column7: Farmers adopting Good Animal Husbandry Practices (GAHPs)
column12: A key PDO indicator counts the number of farmers adopting Good Animal Husbandry Practices as a result of training and extension support, demonstrating uptake of improved practices.

column7: Vulnerable farmers affected by insecurity supported for stock asset replenishment
column12: The results framework includes an indicator counting vulnerable and internally displaced farmers who receive livestock and inputs to replenish their herds, enhancing resilience in conflict‑affected areas.

column7: Direct project beneficiaries (percentage female)
column12: An outcome indicator counts the number of direct project beneficiaries and the percentage of female beneficiaries, aiming to ensure equitable participation and empowerment of women in the livestock sector.

column7: Climate‑friendly livestock master plan developed and integrated animal feed strategy prepared
column12: Intermediate results indicators include development of a climate‑friendly livestock master plan and preparation of an integrated animal feed strategy, reflecting strategic planning and institutional reform.

column7: Percentage of animals vaccinated (cattle, small ruminants, poultry)
column12: Intermediate indicators measure the percentage of cattle, small ruminants and poultry vaccinated against priority diseases, reflecting improved disease control and resilience.

column7: Number of cows inseminated and number of artificial insemination centres rehabilitated
column12: The results framework counts the number of cows inseminated and the number of artificial insemination centres rehabilitated, indicating improvements in genetic quality and productivity.

column7: Number of milk collection centres and slaughterhouses built or rehabilitated
column12: Intermediate indicators record the number of milk collection centres and slaughterhouses built or rehabilitated, improving post‑harvest handling and market efficiency.

column7: Number of business plans co‑financed by the Livestock Improvement Financial Facility and proportion of grants to female farmers
column12: Indicators track the number of business plans co‑financed through the Livestock Improvement Financial Facility and the proportion of grants awarded to female farmers, supporting inclusive financing and enterprise development.

column7: Livestock Market Information System operational and reporting statistics
column12: An intermediate indicator specifies that an integrated Livestock Market Information System (LMIS) should be operational and reporting market statistics, improving transparency and decision‑making.

Increase the quality and utilization of health services with focus on maternal, child and adolescent health, nutrition and disease surveillance
column12: The Project Development Objective is to increase the quality and utilization of health services with a particular focus on maternal, child and adolescent health, nutrition and disease surveillance.

column7: Establish a One Health platform and emergency operations centre for cross‑sectoral disease surveillance coordination
column12: Component 3 supports establishing a national One Health platform and an emergency operations centre to coordinate across ministries of health, agriculture, animal husbandry and environment, enabling rapid cross‑sectoral disease surveillance and response.

column7: Strengthen disease surveillance through interoperable electronic reporting, community surveillance and training of surveillance agents
column12: Subcomponent 3.1 finances improved ICT capacity to establish an interoperable electronic real‑time reporting system, strengthens linkages between national animal and human health surveillance systems, supports community‑level surveillance and trains surveillance agents and veterinary facilities.

column7: Enhance preparedness and emergency response capacity through updated cross‑sectoral plans and training for health professionals
column12: Subcomponent 3.2 strengthens health system preparedness by updating cross‑sectoral emergency preparedness plans for priority zoonotic diseases and food safety and providing training for health professionals in disease surveillance, laboratory biosafety and food safety.

column7: Build institutional capacity through assessments of animal and human health systems and training
column12: Subcomponent 3.3 supports institutional capacity building, financing routine independent assessments of animal and human health capacities using OIE and WHO tools and providing training and project management for One Health implementation.

column7: Multi‑hazard national public health emergency preparedness and response plan implemented
column12: A PDO indicator measures whether a multi‑hazard national public health emergency preparedness and response plan is implemented, signifying strengthened institutional preparedness and cross‑sectoral coordination.

column7: Interoperable electronic real‑time disease reporting system operational
column12: Intermediate indicators include establishment of an interoperable electronic real‑time reporting system linking animal and human health surveillance, demonstrating improved surveillance capacity.

Support government efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and raise mining and livestock productivity, and improve health service delivery
column12: The Program Development Objective is to support government efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and raise mining and livestock productivity, and improve health service delivery and social spending efficiency.

column7: Adopt animal vaccination mechanisms to improve natural resources management and livestock productivity
column12: Under Pillar 2, the operation supports adoption of animal vaccination mechanisms to improve natural resource management and raise mining and livestock productivity, strengthening delivery of animal health services.
column17: Pillar 2: Natural resources management and livestock productivity

column7: Increase in share of small ruminant herd vaccinated against PPR
column12: The expected results matrix includes an increase in the share of small ruminant herd vaccinated against PPR as the key outcome under the pillar on natural resources management and livestock productivity.

column7: Support government efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and livestock productivity and enhance service delivery
column12: The Program Development Objective is to support government efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and livestock productivity, and enhance service delivery and social spending efficiency.

column7: Promote animal vaccination to raise climate resilience and productivity of livestock
column12: Pillar 2 seeks to raise climate resilience and productivity of livestock through adoption of animal vaccination, reducing vulnerability to diseases.

column7: Increase in share of small ruminant herd vaccinated against PPR
column12: The expected results include a greater share of small ruminants vaccinated against PPR, reducing livestock depletion and helping households cope with shocks.

column7: Support government efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and raise mining and livestock productivity, and improve health service delivery
column12: The objective of the First Development Policy Operation is to support the government’s efforts to strengthen fiscal management, improve natural resources management and raise mining and livestock productivity, and improve health service delivery.

column7: Develop mechanisms to expand animal vaccination and public veterinary health
column12: The operation aims to improve productivity in the livestock sector by supporting animal and public veterinary health, including adoption of mechanisms to develop animal vaccination.

column7: Increase in share of small ruminant herd vaccinated against PPR
column12: The expected results matrix includes an increase in the share of small ruminant herd vaccinated against PPR, leading to reduced livestock losses and helping rural households cope with shocks.

column7: Increase agricultural productivity and agribusiness capacity with crisis response
column12: The project development objective (PDO) is to increase agricultural productivity of small-scale farmers, strengthen capacity of micro, small and medium-sized agribusiness enterprises in the project area, and provide immediate and effective response in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

column7: Community-managed productive infrastructure including water points, small-scale irrigation, cattle dips, vaccination centers and early warning systems
column12: The project will finance community-driven subprojects selected through participatory planning processes. Productive community infrastructure includes water points, footpaths, small-scale irrigation or drainage systems, cattle dips, vaccination centers, and community-based early warning systems and communication devices.

column7: Provide matching grants for producer groups to rebuild animal stocks and invest in marketing, processing and conservation of animal products
column12: Producer groups with access to matching grants will be able to rebuild their animal stocks. The project will also finance the development of improved livestock husbandry training material as well as investments in upgrading animal products marketing, processing and conservation infrastructure services and equipment.

column7: Deliver improved livestock husbandry training to producers as part of agribusiness support
column12: Producer groups accessing matching grants will also receive improved livestock husbandry training materials.

column7: Rehabilitate rural roads and markets with agri-logistics services including livestock auctions and storage
column12: This component focuses on ensuring all-season accessibility of selected rural roads and rehabilitating markets with associated agri-logistics services along agriculture trading corridors.

column7: Enhance agriculture public services to deliver climate and nutrition-smart agriculture technologies, plant and animal health advice and vaccines
column12: Agriculture public services will be supported to disseminate climate and nutrition smart agriculture technologies and practices. Services will improve farmer producer group access to climate information, climate smart agriculture advice, plant and animal health advice and vaccines with a gender lens.

column7: Reduction in mortality rate of small stock and chickens
column12: Among the PDO-level results indicators is the reduction in mortality rate of small stock and chickens (percentage).

column7: Number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services (including female and youth)
column12: The results framework includes an indicator for the number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services, disaggregated by gender and youth.

Increase area under sustainable landscape management and promote transboundary collaboration
column12: The Project Development Objective is to increase the area under sustainable landscape management in selected locations in Tajikistan and promote Tajikistan's collaboration with Central Asia countries on transboundary landscape restoration.

column7: Provide sub-grants to Pasture User Unions to prepare and implement pasture management plans with measures for pasture productivity, erosion control, grazing management, animal health and breed improvement
column12: The project will provide sub-grants to Pasture User Unions to support sustainable pasture- and fodder-based livestock production systems. The plans will identify activities to improve pasture productivity, implement erosion and landslide control, improve grazing management and silvo-pastoralism, and include animal health requirements and breed improvement measures.

column7: Establish small climate-resilient facilities such as shelters, feeding stalls, salt licks, sheep baths, vaccination dips and fences, and pens to protect livestock from predators
column12: Pasture management will be complemented by the establishment of small productive and climate-resilient facilities such as shelters, feeding stalls, salt licks, scratching posts, drinking water troughs, sheep baths, and fences to enhance animal welfare and improve the productivity and resilience of livestock systems. Protected area management includes pilot measures to resolve human-wildlife conflicts, such as pens to protect livestock from predators.
column19: Component 2; Pasture/Livestock Management Plans and Protected Area Management

column7: Area brought under pasture management plans
column12: The results framework lists an indicator for the area brought under pasture management plans, with a target of 83,000 hectares.

column7: Number of persons trained on integrated landscape management, segregated by women
column12: The results framework includes an indicator for the number of persons trained in central and local government units on integrated landscape management and related subjects, segregated by central, local and women, with a target of 550.

column7: Share of sub-grants disbursed to women-led groups and women participation in decision-making roles
column12: The results framework specifies that 15 percent of sub-grants will be disbursed to women-led or predominantly women groups and that 50 percent of pasture user unions or community groups will have women members in decision-making roles.

column7: Improve One Health coordination and address capacity gaps to prevent, detect and respond to zoonotic diseases, AMR and food safety risks
column12: The proposed development objective is to improve One Health coordination and address key cross-sectoral capacity gaps to prevent, detect, and respond to key zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and food safety risks in participating countries.

column7: Establish national and regional One Health coordination structures and incorporate One Health into legislative and regulatory frameworks
column12: Component 1 will establish a regional One Health coordinating structure with a steering committee, technical committees and working groups on zoonotic diseases, food safety and AMR. National One Health mechanisms will coordinate communication with policymakers and guide implementation. Subcomponent 1c will incorporate One Health into legislative and regulatory frameworks by reviewing and updating legislation and strengthening regulatory agencies to inspect and enforce PPR, zoonotic disease, AMR and food safety standards.

column7: Develop a regional One Health research and training center, conduct assessments and studies, and build multisector workforce capacity through training and education on zoonotic diseases, AMR and food safety
column12: Component 2 will address knowledge and workforce capacity needs by establishing a Regional One Health Research, Education and Training Center, conducting risk assessments and epidemiological modeling to predict disease outbreaks, establishing partnerships for research, and disseminating knowledge. It will develop a multisector workforce strategy, mainstream One Health in sectoral education programs, and provide on-the-job training for professionals in agriculture, veterinary, environment and human health sectors.

column7: Strengthen cross-sectoral surveillance, prevention and response systems for zoonotic diseases, AMR and food hazards and equip wildlife rangers and border points
column12: Component 3 will strengthen One Health surveillance, laboratories and data systems. Subcomponent 3a will develop cross-sectoral animal, ecosystem and human health systems for early detection and response to zoonotic diseases, AMR and foodborne illnesses, establish epidemiology units, implement cross-sectoral early warning surveillance, carry out prevention and response activities based on risk assessments, equip wildlife rangers for sampling and cold equipment, and establish quarantine and border security with designated points of entry implementing routine core capacities.

column7: Develop national and regional laboratory networks for diagnosis of zoonotic diseases, AMR and food safety
column12: Subcomponent 3b will develop, renovate and equip priority laboratory facilities at local, national and regional levels for sampling, testing, data management and reporting of zoonotic diseases, AMR and food safety hazards; adapt and implement international standard operating procedures; and develop networks of accredited reference laboratories.

column7: Strengthened surveillance and diagnostic capacity using a One Health approach
column12: The development objective and key results indicate that the project aims to strengthen surveillance and diagnostic capacity in participating countries using a One Health approach.

column7: Strengthen surveillance and diagnostic capacity in OECS countries through a One Health approach
column12: The development objective is to strengthen surveillance and diagnostic capacity in the selected four OECS countries through the implementation of a One Health approach.

column7: Strengthen multisectoral surveillance systems and response for zoonosis, AMR and emerging health threats
column12: Component 1 will strengthen multisectoral surveillance systems and responses for zoonosis, antimicrobial resistance and other emerging health threats by improving early warning systems, surveillance reporting completeness and quality across animal and human health sectors, developing joint preparedness and response plans and protocols, and enhancing port health protocols and incident management plans.

column7: Strengthen regional diagnostic capacity through provision of consumables, equipment and maintenance plans for human and animal laboratories
column12: The project will focus on strengthening human and animal laboratories by providing critical consumables, materials and machines for diagnostic tests and generating essential maintenance plans. Where animal laboratories do not exist, alternative mechanisms such as access to a regional laboratory will be established, and the project will contribute to regional diagnostic networks.

column7: Train health, veterinary and laboratory staff and establish antimicrobial stewardship programs
column12: The project will provide training for ministry staff in laboratory management, diagnostic tests, sample collection and packaging for zoonotic and AMR threats, epidemiology and outbreak investigation. It will establish a functional antimicrobial stewardship program and provide capacity building for laboratory services.

column7: Surveillance and diagnostic capacity strengthened using a One Health approach
column12: The key results section states that the surveillance and diagnostic capacity of the selected four OECS countries is strengthened using a One Health approach through the implementation of the Pandemic Fund.

column7: Restore agricultural livelihoods and enhance climate resilience for farmers and fisherfolk
column12: "The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to contribute to restoring agricultural livelihoods and enhancing climate resilience of farmers and fisherfolk affected by Hurricane Maria in Dominica."

column7: Restoration of livestock production base and climate‑resilient animal housing
column11: poultry; goats; sheep; rabbits; pigs; bees
column12: The project finances procurement of inputs and technical advisory services for livestock farmers and fisherfolk. It supports about 200 livestock producers (20 % women) to reestablish their production base after Hurricane Maria by investing in restoration of damaged animal shelter/housing and other infrastructure for poultry (layers and broilers), goats, sheep, rabbits and pigs, and beekeeping, ensuring climate‑resilient specifications and co‑financing.

column7: Rehabilitation of public agriculture infrastructure (Central Livestock Farm, propagation centres)
column12: Subcomponent B.1 restores key public infrastructure and assets damaged by the hurricane. Reconstruction focuses on five crop propagation centers, a Central Livestock Farm (CLF), MAF regional offices and training centres, forestry facilities, eco‑trails, and community irrigation systems. The infrastructure will be rebuilt using resilient construction standards and improved safety specifications to reduce climate and weather risks.

column7: Institutional strengthening of Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries
column12: Subcomponent B.2 provides capacity‑building assistance to the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries. It finances consulting services, training, analytical studies and development of information systems to revise policies and regulatory frameworks, support agricultural census, develop an e‑agriculture strategy, integrated sector management information systems, insurance models for fisheries, agribusiness strategies and other institutional strengthening activities.

column7: Farmers with restored climate‑resilient livestock infrastructure
column11: poultry; goats; sheep; rabbits; pigs; bees
column12: The results framework includes an indicator counting farmers with restored infrastructure for livestock production, including climate‑resilient animal houses. The baseline is zero and the end target is 200 farmers, with 20 % female farmers. Climate‑resilient animal houses apply storm‑resistant standards such as roof member connector straps.

column7: Farmers adopting improved agricultural technologies
column12: The results framework lists farmers adopting improved agricultural technologies promoted by the project. The baseline is zero and the end target is 3,600 farmers (20 % women), indicating adoption of improved technologies and practices, including climate‑resilient innovations.

column7: Increase agricultural productivity and improve marketing of crops and animal products in targeted areas
column12: The proposed Project Development Objective for the additional financing is to increase agricultural productivity and improve marketing of crops and animal products in targeted areas.

column7: Improved agricultural and animal production with mixed farming and extension services
column12: Component 1 consolidates and develops activities to increase the capacity of smallholder farmers to produce staple crops and small stock, including chicken. It extends the program to additional territories and perennial crops, promotes mixed farming systems, revamps extension and advisory services, introduces climate adaptation technologies, supports micro‑projects for storage facilities, warehouses, processing centres and nurseries, and expands a matching grant facility combined with free technical assistance.

column7: Rehabilitation of feeder roads and local markets with storage facilities
column12: Component 2 aims to continue rehabilitation and maintenance of feeder roads and construction of key local markets and storage facilities across three provinces. It focuses on building capacity at local and provincial levels to ensure that infrastructure investments are maintained and sustainable.

column7: Re-engineering agricultural extension services and strengthening R&D and planning
column12: Component 3 supports the government’s efforts to re‑engineer national agricultural extension and advisory services, strengthen planning, coordination and monitoring and evaluation at national and provincial levels, and strengthen agricultural research and development for efficiency and effectiveness gains.

column7: Increase in productivity of crops and animal products
column12: The project’s objective is to increase agricultural productivity of staple crops and small stock, including chicken, in targeted areas. Enhancing productivity is a key intended outcome of the additional financing.

column7: Improved marketing of crops and animal products
column12: The PDO specifies improving marketing of crops and animal products by smallholder farmers in targeted areas. Investments in feeder roads, local markets and storage facilities aim to enhance market efficiency for agricultural and livestock products.

column7: Improve productivity and profitability of smallholder agriculture in selected areas of Timor-Leste
column12: The Sustainable Agriculture Productivity Improvement Project aims to improve productivity and profitability of smallholder agriculture in selected areas of Timor‑Leste through adoption of improved technologies and management practices.

column7: Livestock control infrastructure for controlled grazing, feeding and fodder management
column12: Subcomponent 3.3 (Technologies and small-scale works for sustainable watershed/sub‑watershed management) supports procurement and distribution of seeds, small‑scale equipment and technologies. It includes livestock control/management infrastructure for controlled grazing and improved feeding and fodder management, helping communities adopting stall feeding and penning instead of free grazing.

column7: Increase in share of total production sold on the market
column12: The results framework includes an indicator “Increase in share of total production sold on the market” which tracks the proportion of crop and livestock production that is marketed. This outcome measures improvements in market participation for agricultural and livestock products.

column7: Farmers adopting improved agricultural technology promoted by the project
column12: The results framework lists the number of farmers who have adopted improved agricultural technology promoted by the project. Targets increase from 3,300 to 16,500 farmers over the life of the project, reflecting adoption of improved technologies and practices.

column7: Protect livelihoods and restore agricultural and pastoral production in locust‑affected countries
column12: Component 2 of the program aims to protect poor and vulnerable households in locust‑affected areas, safeguard them from human capital and asset loss, and rehabilitate food production systems and livelihoods damaged by locust swarms, reflecting the objective of protecting livelihoods and restoring agricultural and pastoral production.

column7: Emergency cash transfers and fodder provision for livestock holding households
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 provides emergency income support (cash transfers and cash‑for‑work) to vulnerable households in locust‑affected areas. It includes fodder provision to livestock holding households to replace impacted grazing land until restoration is completed, ensuring livestock survive while pastures recover.

column7: Pasture restoration, temporary feed provision and restocking with climate‑resilient breeds
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 supports affected farmers and livestock holding households to restore their productive assets. It delivers climate‑smart farmer packets, restores pasture or provides temporary forage/feed, implements climate‑resilient grazing management in pastoral areas, and assists with animal restocking using climate‑resilient and stress‑tolerant breeds.

column7: Affected livestock holding households receiving emergency fodder
column12: The results framework includes an indicator tracking the number of affected livestock holding households receiving emergency fodder. The baseline is zero and the end target is 1,000 households, reflecting support to maintain livestock during the locust crisis.

column7: Affected livestock holding households receiving replacement livestock
column12: Another results framework indicator counts the number of affected livestock holding households receiving replacement livestock. The baseline is zero and the end target is 1,000 households, indicating restoration of livestock assets after locust damage.

column7: Protect livelihoods and restore food and livestock production and strengthen preparedness against locust outbreaks
column12: The project aims to help farm and livestock households return to production for improved food security, restore biodiversity and strengthen preparedness against future locust outbreaks through integrated land use systems, agroforestry and livelihood support.

column7: Integrated agroforestry and silvopastoral systems with fodder banks and pasture management
column12: Subcomponent 2.3 invests in land use systems that integrate crops, trees and livestock to restore biodiversity and enhance resilience. Communities plant multipurpose trees for fodder, fuel and construction materials; establish nurseries, community woodlots and fodder banks; and develop rotational grazing and pasture management plans. Training on Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration and silvopastoral practices builds capacity for sustainable agro‑ecological systems.

column7: Emergency fodder/feed and agro‑forestry support for affected livestock households
column12: The livelihoods protection and rehabilitation component provides emergency fodder/feed to affected livestock holding households and supports agro‑forestry interventions. It delivers input packets to affected farmers and invests in community nurseries and agro‑forestry, enabling households to access fodder and feed and diversify their livelihoods.

column7: Locust‑affected farmers reporting renewed agricultural activity
column12: The results framework reports the number of locust‑affected farmers, including livestock owners and beekeepers, who report renewed agricultural activity. The baseline is zero and end targets increase to 135,000, indicating recovery of livelihoods after the locust crisis.

column7: Affected livestock holding households receiving emergency fodder/feed
column12: Intermediate results indicators include the number of affected livestock holding households receiving emergency fodder/feed. The baseline is zero and end target is 20,000 households, with 12,000 female‑headed households receiving emergency fodder/feed.

column7: Strengthen Guyana’s capacities to prevent, prepare and respond to health emergencies through a One Health approach
column12: The proposed development objective is to strengthen Guyana’s capacities to prevent, prepare and respond to health emergencies through a One Health approach and, in the case of an eligible crisis or emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

column7: Enhancing diagnostic capacity and laboratory systems for zoonotic and animal diseases
column12: Component 1 enhances Guyana’s national laboratory network. It focuses on procurement of laboratory infrastructure and diagnostic capacity, integration of laboratory systems, biosafety improvements, and workforce development to improve detection of AMR, zoonotic, vector‑borne and environmental health threats.

column7: Digital and multisectoral health surveillance systems for zoonotic disease detection
column12: Component 2 strengthens health surveillance systems for early detection and response. It integrates digital infrastructure and develops multisectoral health surveillance systems, building workforce and operational capacity to detect and respond rapidly to zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, vector‑borne and environmental health threats.

column7: Strengthening cross‑sectoral One Health coordination, awareness and training
column12: Component 3 enhances cross‑sectoral collaboration among human, animal and environmental health sectors. It formalizes structured coordination, builds institutional capacities, raises public awareness and conducts training and capacity building in One Health to improve resilience to health and climate‑related emergencies.

column7: Integrated public health laboratory networks and data‑driven surveillance system
column12: Key results include establishing integrated and digitized public health laboratory networks and a rapid, data‑driven health surveillance system to enable timely decision‑making and improved prevention and response to health threats, including priority zoonotic diseases.

column7: Strengthened multisectoral One Health coordination and workforce capacity
column12: The key results describe strengthened public health workforce, enhanced border security with digitized health systems, improved healthcare equity, and strengthened multisectoral capacity to prevent, detect and respond to health emergencies through better collaboration between human, animal and environmental health sectors.

column7: increase productivity and commercialization of producers and processors in selected value chains, strengthen service delivery systems in the livestock and fisheries sectors, and respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency
column12: The datasheet states that the project aims to increase productivity and commercialization of producers and processors in selected value chains, strengthen service delivery systems in the livestock and fisheries sectors, and respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency

column7: Enabling sub-projects implementation and preparatory analyses
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Advisory & Extension; Markets & Finance
column12: Activities include preparatory studies, beneficiary identification, training of development agents, and feasibility studies for establishing a line of credit to enable implementation of sub-projects and monitor beneficiary transformation.

column7: Support to subsistence farmers and unemployed youth
column12: Finances basic sub-projects for subsistence farmers and unemployed youth by establishing primary cooperatives, providing training and advisory services, inputs, equipment, and small infrastructure to master minimum good practices (Eth-GAP1).

column7: Support to improved cooperatives
column12: Provides intermediate sub-projects linking cooperatives with buyers through formal contracts, offering training, inputs, services and infrastructure to improve production intensity and organization using Eth-GAP2.

column7: Support to specialized cooperatives and municipalities
column12: Implements advanced sub-projects connecting value-chain actors via formal contracts, providing specialized training, advisory services, inputs, equipment, and medium-scale infrastructure targeting specialized cooperatives and municipalities.

column7: Human resources and organizational capacity development

column12: Supports rehabilitation of training facilities, provision of transport and equipment, partnerships between public authorities and private veterinarians, enhanced surveillance and diagnostics, and improved extension services promoting GAHP and GAFP.

column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Policy & Regulatory; Public Health
column12: Supports national programs: animal identification and traceability system, animal disease prevention/control (Newcastle disease, PPR), national feed/forage program, national breeding program, and aquaculture and fisheries master plan.

column7: Project coordination, monitoring and evaluation, and knowledge management
column12: Finances project coordination and management across federal, regional and Woreda levels, including staff, consultants, operating costs, equipment, audits and training to strengthen institutional arrangements.

column7: Productivity
column12: The results framework lists a PDO-level indicator measuring change in productivity of small-scale producers by selected commodity, reflecting intended productivity improvements.

column7: Market efficiency
column12: An indicator measures increase in sales of primary and processed livestock and fish products by producers and processors, indicating improved commercialization and market efficiency.

column7: Institutional reforms
column12: PDO indicators count the number of system improvements supporting better livestock and fisheries service delivery, such as rationalizing veterinary services, improving extension services, and implementing identification and traceability systems.

column7: Adoption
column12: The results framework monitors the proportion of trainees applying newly acquired competencies in their daily work, reflecting adoption of new skills and practices.

column7: Resilience
column12: A PDO indicator tracks the time lapse between early warning information and disbursement toward response during crises or emergencies, indicating enhanced resilience and rapid response capacity.

column12: Implements community-based initiatives for herders to improve veterinary service delivery and compliance with disease control, using risk assessment tools and promoting women’s leadership in animal health activities.

column8: Markets & Finance; Livestock Management & Technologies; Food Processing & Storage; Behavior Change & Social Programs

column7: Improve productivity, commercialization, and resilience of targeted livestock production systems in Nigeria
column12: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to “improve productivity, commercialization, and resilience of targeted livestock production systems in Nigeria”

column7: Policy formulation, planning and capacity strengthening
column12: Sub‑component 1.1 finances a comprehensive Livestock Master Plan, digital data tools, and sub‑sector policies for feeding, breeding, dairy and animal health. It provides scholarships and capacity‑building programs and mainstreams climate change adaptation and mitigation objectives in sector policies.

column7: Genetic resource management and Good Animal Husbandry support
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Sub‑component 1.2 develops and implements a genetic resource management strategy prioritizing large ruminants; rehabilitates and equips artificial insemination and breed improvement centers; trains extension agents and produces digital guides and Farmer Field Schools on Good Animal Husbandry Practices; promotes improved feed production and storage, feeding and grazing practices, and trains state‑level extension agents while addressing gender gaps.

column7: Strengthening national animal health services
column8: Public Health; Livestock Management & Technologies; Policy & Regulatory
column12: Sub‑component 1.3 strengthens national veterinary services by supporting private veterinary service development, financing infrastructure and equipment (including solar‑powered cold chains) for disease surveillance, diagnostics and control, improving quality control for veterinary medicines, establishing One‑Health platforms and collaborating with the private sector to expand vaccine production.

column7: Market linkages and climate‑smart livestock infrastructure
column8: Markets & Finance; Food Processing & Storage; Rural/Public Infrastructure; Advisory & Extension
column12: Sub‑component 2.1 organizes producers into cooperatives and provides training and advisory services. It finances milking and cooling equipment, transport and storage assets, establishes climate‑smart livestock markets with water sources, weighbridges, paddocks and veterinary outposts, rehabilitates abattoirs and introduces online market information systems, with specific support for women’s participation.

column7: Access to finance and risk‑sharing facility
column8: Markets & Finance; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Sub‑component 2.2 finances a credit line and risk‑sharing facility to de‑risk climate‑smart livestock investments across beef, dairy, sheep, goat, pig and poultry value chains; provides technical assistance to participating financial institutions and supports business development services while targeting gender gaps in access to finance.

column7: Livestock Service Centers (LSCs)
column8: Rural/Public Infrastructure; Livestock Management & Technologies; Food Processing & Storage; Advisory & Extension
column11: cattle; dairy; small ruminants; pigs; poultry
column12: Sub‑component 2.3 supports the design and establishment of Livestock Service Centers in gazetted grazing reserves to promote commercialization and reduce open grazing. It finances training centers, veterinary facilities, breeding and artificial insemination services, markets, digital information systems, milk collection and cooling centers, water points, input outlets and grazing areas, ensuring gender‑friendly facilities and service hours.

column7: Natural resources management and pasture improvement
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Ecosystem Services; Rural/Public Infrastructure
column12: Sub‑component 3.1 invests in climate‑smart rangeland and pasture management by assessing water and feed resources via remote sensing, disseminating information to herders, organizing community processes to improve grazing practices, constructing or rehabilitating stock routes and water points, and developing cultivated pasture with irrigation, thereby increasing carbon sequestration and reducing methane emissions.

column7: Conflict mitigation and resource management
column8: Behavior Change & Social Programs; Policy & Regulatory; Markets & Finance
column12: Sub‑component 3.2 establishes and trains local committees for conflict prevention and resolution, supports community dialogue on equitable resource use, finances small‑scale infrastructure such as corridors, rest areas, stock routes, shelters and feed storage, develops early warning systems with remote sensing, supports policy dialogue on grazing reserves and transhumance rules, conducts feasibility studies for livestock insurance and facilitates transboundary dialogue with neighboring countries.

column7: Project coordination, monitoring and management
column8: Policy & Regulatory; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Component 4 establishes national and state coordination offices and supports planning, monitoring and evaluation, procurement and fiduciary management, eligibility assessments, social risk mitigation (including gender and GBV), knowledge management and communication strategies to ensure effective project implementation.

column7: Contingent emergency response
column12: Component 5 is a zero‑dollar Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) that allows reallocation of project funds to respond promptly to crises such as disasters, conflict or disease outbreaks, covering mitigation, recovery and reconstruction activities upon World Bank approval.

The results framework defines a PDO‑level indicator measuring the percentage increase in productivity of livestock species in targeted production systems, expressed through carcass weight and milk yield.

The PDO indicators include the share of beneficiary livestock producers’ stock that is marketed and the share of target beneficiaries rating “Satisfied” or above on the process and impact of project interventions, reflecting improved commercialization and customer satisfaction.
The results framework tracks the number of farmers adopting climate‑smart technologies and the number adopting improved agricultural technologies, indicating adoption of enhanced practices.

The project monitors the reduced incidence of resource‑based farmer‑herder conflicts and the share of beneficiaries satisfied with project interventions, indicators that capture improvements in community cohesion and social inclusion.
A PDO indicator counts the number of direct project beneficiaries disaggregated by sex, highlighting inclusivity and gender considerations in project participation.

column7: Develop water and agricultural services among agro‑pastoralist communities in dry‑land areas of Somalia
column12: The proposed Project Development Objective (PDO) is to develop water and agricultural services among agro‑pastoralist communities in dry‑land areas of Somalia.

column7: Construction of new community water points
column8: Rural/Public Infrastructure; Ecosystem Services; Advisory & Extension
column12: Component 1 finances development of multiple‑use water resources, constructing new community water points such as sand and subsurface dams in dry river beds, surface water storage structures like berkads and hafir dams, semicircular bunds, soil bunds, rock catchments, and uses solar pumps to supply water for human consumption, livestock and irrigation.

column7: Rehabilitation of existing community water points
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 rehabilitates existing water infrastructure, including boreholes, and extends facilities to ensure multiple‑use water supply by refurbishing sand dams, berkads and other structures while integrating catchment protection and infiltration measures to increase water storage capacity and resilience to droughts.

column7: National and state institutional capacity building
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 strengthens national and state institutions to plan, implement and monitor integrated agriculture and water development programs by developing construction standards, rangeland management guidelines, environmental impact assessments, engineering and hydrological studies, and providing improved extension services and data systems for farmers and pastoralists.

column7: Community development and demand mobilization
column8: Behavior Change & Social Programs; Advisory & Extension; Policy & Regulatory
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 uses community dialogue to mobilize and plan water and livelihood interventions, increases awareness of proposed investments, and develops community development plans ensuring equitable representation of women and youth and sustainable resource management.

column7: Integrated landscape management
column12: Under Component 3, integrated landscape management activities include soil and water conservation structures, terracing, gully rehabilitation, tree planting, rotational grazing, alternative energy sources and community orchards to restore degraded land and increase resilience.

column7: Agriculture and livestock support
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: The project supports agriculture and livestock production by establishing community gardens, providing improved seeds, micro‑irrigation technologies, soil nutrient assessments, training on climate‑smart farming, fodder production, improved animal health services and kitchen gardens.

column7: Project management, M&E and CERC
column12: Component 4 supports project management units, monitoring and evaluation, knowledge management and learning systems. It establishes web‑based management information systems, uses geotagging and flood mapping, supports continuous learning and includes a Contingent Emergency Response subcomponent to reallocate funds quickly during crises.

A PDO‑level indicator measures the number of people provided with access to improved water sources, with half of them female, reflecting improved access to safe water for domestic use, livestock and irrigation.
Another PDO indicator counts farmers or clients adopting improved technology (number and percent women), capturing adoption of improved agricultural and livestock practices promoted by the project.

The results framework includes the percentage of target beneficiaries satisfied with project investments, reflecting community perceptions and social cohesion resulting from participatory planning and equitable resource access.

Intermediate results indicators track the number of improved community water points constructed or rehabilitated, aiming to strengthen community resilience to droughts and floods by improving water availability.

Indicators measure the number of Project Implementation Units established and functioning with 50 percent female staff, the number of community management systems established, the number of PIU members trained (male and female) and the percentage of farmers/clients reached with agricultural services who are women.

column7: Develop water, agriculture, and environmental services for rural communities in Somalia’s drylands
column12: The PDO is to develop water, agriculture, and environmental services for rural communities in Somalia’s drylands.

column7: Development of multiuse water sources
column8: Rural/Public Infrastructure; Ecosystem Services; Policy & Regulatory; Advisory & Extension
column12: Component 1 constructs climate‑resilient multiuse water infrastructure such as sand and subsurface dams, surface storage structures (berkads, hafir dams, balleys) and boreholes; uses solar pumps and gravity‑fed systems; and integrates catchment protection and climate‑resilience measures to provide water for domestic use, farming and livestock. It also provides institutional and capacity development for water service institutions, including water sharing agreements, site selection tools and O&M guidelines, and pilots innovative decision support tools.

column7: Sustainable farming production and development
column8: Crop Management & Technology; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 introduces technologies, innovations and management practices (TIMPs) to improve water use efficiency and climate‑smart agriculture, such as micro‑irrigation systems, drought‑tolerant seeds, balanced soil fertility management, integrated pest management, conservation agriculture and solar pumping. It mobilizes farmers into Common Interest Groups and Farmer Producer Organizations with emphasis on female‑led groups, establishes demonstration plots and farmer field schools, and provides micro‑project grants for irrigation development, sustainable land management, vulnerable groups and nutrition mainstreaming.

column7: Sustainable livestock production and development
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 supports pastoralist communities with improved grazing management, climate‑smart livestock production assets, extension services and female‑targeted training. It trains female extension agents and veterinarians, forms inclusive cooperatives and self‑help groups, establishes pastoralist field schools, and provides micro‑project grants for improved drought‑tolerant breeds, dairy farming, animal finishing, fodder production, animal health and disease control.

column7: Agricultural and livestock extension ecosystem and digital agriculture
column8: Advisory & Extension; Technology & R&D; Policy & Regulatory; Markets & Finance; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Subcomponent 2.3 builds a coherent agriculture and livestock extension ecosystem by combining public, private and community‑led services, linking research to extension, and supporting digital agriculture. It pilots geo‑tagged farmer registration, digital delivery of priority TIMPs, e‑extension services, solar‑powered irrigation systems, access to finance and market information, and targeted support for women and youth as e‑extension providers.

column7: Environmental catchment services and rangeland restoration
column12: Component 3 restores ecosystems and enhances resilience to extreme climate events. It promotes rangeland restoration, sustainable land management, vegetation cover and riverbank protection, invests in water harvesting and soil conservation, and strengthens the capacity of environmental institutions, aiming to increase vegetation cover, improve soil moisture and mitigate drought and flood impacts.

column7: Project management, community development and livelihoods planning
column8: Policy & Regulatory; Advisory & Extension; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Component 4 integrates project management with community development and livelihood planning, supporting institutional strengthening, participatory planning, capacity development and livelihood strategies to ensure that water, agriculture and environmental services translate into sustainable livelihoods and resilience.

One PDO‑level indicator measures the number of people provided with access to improved water sources (with the proportion of females), signifying improved access to safe water for households, livestock and irrigation.

Another PDO indicator counts farmers adopting improved agricultural technology, with a separate count for female farmers, measuring adoption of climate‑smart agricultural practices facilitated by the project.

column9: Soil health and land use change
column12: A PDO‑level indicator tracks the land area under sustainable landscape management practices (hectares), reflecting adoption of sustainable land management and catchment restoration activities.

The project’s implementation strategy and indicators emphasize women’s employment in technical and managerial roles in water and agriculture institutions and participation in Common Interest Groups and field schools, highlighting efforts to increase women’s empowerment and inclusion.

column7: Promote adoption of improved production practices by target farmers with gradual rollout of farmer-centric agricultural service systems and investment support
column12: The original Project Development Objective is to promote adoption of improved production practices by target farmers, with gradual rollout of farmer-centric agricultural services systems and investment support.

column7: Improved animal health service delivery
column8: Public Health; Livestock Management & Technologies; Policy & Regulatory
column12: Subcomponent 2.a of the Animal Production and Health component ensures that the government assumes responsibility for the Sanitary Mandate Contracting Scheme and establishes National Animal Disease Control Programs, starting with brucellosis and expanding to foot‑and‑mouth disease and Peste des Petits Ruminants. It strengthens veterinary services and supports a public‑private partnership for the Afghanistan Vaccine Production Laboratory to increase vaccine production.

column7: Improved animal production through investment packages
column8: Livestock Management & Technologies; Food Processing & Storage; Markets & Finance; Behavior Change & Social Programs; Public Health
column12: Subcomponent 2.b finances 400 investment packages for the livestock sector covering poultry development (testing productive breeds, introducing concentrated feeds and thermostable Newcastle Disease vaccines, semi‑commercial layer and broiler packages benefiting 30,000 women with 30‑bird packages and 5,000 women with 100‑bird packages), fish farming and aquaculture expansion through pilot enterprises and fingerling supply, dairy development supporting peri‑urban producer groups and milk collection centers, beekeeping support for 500 farmers, and improvements to small ruminant production through vaccination, supplementary feeding, rangeland management, and fodder banks.

column7: Improved market access and value addition for livestock products
column8: Markets & Finance; Food Processing & Storage; Rural/Public Infrastructure; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Subcomponent 2.c promotes the vaccine value chain through training and information campaigns, supports private poultry input and service delivery networks, develops marketing infrastructure for fish farming and beekeeping (cold chain, slaughter and packaging facilities), strengthens dairy value chains through quality control, milk collection and cooling systems, and develops collaborative frameworks for small ruminant marketing with improved finishing and supplementary feeding.

column7: Implementation management and technical assistance support
column8: Advisory & Extension; Policy & Regulatory; Behavior Change & Social Programs
column12: Component 3 supports implementation management at national and regional levels, providing technical assistance for management, procurement, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, communication, capacity building of the Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock (MAIL), and coordination with donors, ensuring decentralized service delivery systems.

Over 300,000 farmers and herders will directly benefit from improved production and post‑harvest practices through a strengthened extension and learning network, increased delivery capacity of MAIL and support to develop policies and strategies.

The additional financing plans to develop 1,000 productive investment packages for farmers and herders, including orchards, post‑harvesting facilities, improved water use efficiency, fish ponds, backyard poultry keeping, improved animal health, and productivity enhancements, indicating adoption of improved technologies.

The poultry development program will continue semi‑commercial layer and broiler production packages, benefiting 30,000 women with 30‑bird packages and 5,000 women with 100‑bird packages, supporting women’s economic empowerment in livestock activities.

The promotion of vaccination and the vaccine value‑chain aims to reduce mortality of small ruminants from 25 percent to at least 10 percent and village poultry mortality from more than 50 percent to 20–25 percent, reflecting improved animal health outcomes.

column7: Support the development of a seafood cluster in Nouadhibou that promotes sustainable management of fisheries and generates value for the communities
column12: The project’s objective is to support the development of a seafood cluster in Nouadhibou that promotes sustainable management of fisheries and generates value for the communities, ensuring that fish landed in Nouadhibou originates from sustainably managed fisheries and that post‑harvest processing minimizes pollution.

column7: Promoting public‑private dialogue and cluster vision (Subcomponent 1.1)
column8: Policy & Regulatory; Markets & Finance; Advisory & Extension
column12: Subcomponent 1.1 fosters a public‑private dialogue to develop a holistic vision for a sustainable seafood cluster in Nouadhibou, clarifying concepts such as sustainability of fish resources, rights and responsibilities, inclusiveness, transparency and competitiveness. It finances consultants’ services and stakeholder training to design a cluster strategy, identify target value chains, prepare master and investment plans, and develop legal and institutional frameworks and tools such as geographic information systems and M&E for the cluster.

column7: Improving investment climate and PPP framework (Subcomponent 1.1 thematic areas)
column12: Within Subcomponent 1.1, the project addresses nationwide thematic areas critical to the cluster’s development by improving the investment climate and establishing a public‑private partnership framework. It provides technical assistance to the Nouadhibou Free Zone Authority and Ministry of Economy and Finance to develop legal and regulatory frameworks and reduces investment restrictions, supports public‑private dialogue processes and promotes reforms to foster responsible private investment in the fisheries sector.

column7: Generating responsible investments (Subcomponent 1.2)
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 carries out activities to build implementation capacity of Nouadhibou Free Zone stakeholders and to attract responsible private investors through public‑private partnerships. It promotes investment opportunities in the seafood cluster, ensuring that fisheries management plans and total allowable catch regulations are integrated into cluster design and that private participation supports sustainable fisheries.

column7: Improving fish landing and export infrastructure (Subcomponent 2.1)
column8: Rural/Public Infrastructure; Food Processing & Storage; Markets & Finance
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 aims to improve fish landing and export infrastructure by enhancing operational efficiency at the commercial port (PAN) and the artisanal and coastal fishing port (EPBR), constructing a refrigerated warehouse at Nouadhibou International Airport, and providing technical assistance to modernize trade services and increase fresh fish exports. These investments improve handling of landed fish, reduce post‑harvest losses and facilitate trade.

column7: Building local suppliers’ and vulnerable groups’ capacities (Subcomponent 2.2)
column8: Behavior Change & Social Programs; Advisory & Extension; Markets & Finance
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 strengthens the capacity of small‑scale fishers, women, less‑educated and marginalized populations to participate in the seafood value chains by promoting acceptance of fisheries management plans, providing training and capacity building, and improving post‑harvest fish handling. It ensures inclusive participation in the cluster and aims to increase incomes of those engaged in post‑harvest activities.

PDO‑level results indicators include investments generated from responsible investors and increases in the volume of fresh fish exports, capturing improvements in market efficiency and commercialization.
The PDO indicators include the number of direct project beneficiaries and the proportion of female beneficiaries, highlighting inclusivity and the participation of women in the seafood sector.

column12: On‑Farm Landscape Mainstreaming includes recovery of degraded pastures, training of field technicians in ABC technologies, establishment of demonstration units, seed warehouses and technical assistance for integrated crop‑livestock‑forestry systems.

column12: The project management component includes technical coordination, financial management, training and monitoring and evaluation of project activities.

column12: Results indicators cover the number of people attending training, land registered in environmental cadastre, and institutions receiving capacity building support.

column7: Strengthen climate resilience and enabling environment for agriculture development
column12: Program Development Objective: to strengthen the climate resilience and enabling environment for agriculture development in selected value chains in Jordan.

column7: Policy reforms to enhance climate resilience and competitiveness
column12: Results areas include: supporting reforms to strengthen the resilience of agricultural production systems and improving competitiveness and export opportunities by strengthening the enabling environment for agribusiness and addressing on-/off‑farm constraints.

column12: The results framework aims to strengthen climate resilience and sustainability of agriculture and to improve competitiveness and export by addressing enabling environment and production constraints.

column7: Promote adoption of improved production practices by target farmers
column12: The Development Objective of the Project is to promote adoption of improved production practices by target farmers, with gradual rollout of farmer-centric agricultural services systems and investment support.

column7: Horticulture extension, farmer field schools and investment packages
column12: Farmers are organized into common-interest groups and farmer field schools; Farmer Learning & Resource Centers are established; training covers orchard management, IPM, intercropping, vegetable production and water management. Investment packages support rehabilitating orchards, new orchards, vegetable and fruit production, kitchen gardening, saffron demonstrations and women-focused activities such as vegetable processing and mushroom production.

column7: Animal health services and disease control programs
column12: The project will take over the Sanitary Mandate Contracting Scheme and implement national animal disease control programs for brucellosis, FMD and PPR, and support the Afghanistan Vaccine Production Laboratory through investment and management changes.

column7: Investment packages for poultry, fish farming, dairy, beekeeping and small ruminants

column7: Market access and value‑addition for livestock products
column12: Market access subcomponent promotes vaccination distribution networks, development of private poultry service networks, cold chain and processing for fish and honey, quality control and cool storage systems for dairy products, and collaborative frameworks for marketing small ruminant products.
