column12: Key results include raising the average lactation period milk yield per cow at least 10 percent and increasing annual farm household income from milk sales at least 10 percent among project beneficiaries.

column7: Adoption of improved livestock practices
column12: The key results include achieving at least 8,000 farm households adopting improved animal feeding, health, breeding, and management practices, supported by on‑farm demonstrations of climate‑smart practices and technologies.

column7: Women’s economic participation through poultry packages
column12: Investment packages will support 400 poultry packages with improved breeds and feed and vaccination for women – thirty-thousand women will benefit from a 30-bird package and five-thousand women from a 100-bird package.

column7: Improved market access and value addition
column12: The project plans to distribute post‑harvest tools to 10,681 farmers, establish over 350 improved raisin drying houses, train about 100 traders, and link producer groups with processors through improved marketing frameworks.

column7: Develop a sustainable seafood cluster in Nouadhibou
column12: PDO: to support development of a seafood cluster in Nouadhibou that promotes sustainable management of fisheries and generates value for communities.

column7: Public‑private dialogue and cluster strategy
column12: Component 1 includes organizing public‑private dialogue to prepare a vision for the cluster, strengthen capacity of stakeholders, develop a holistic cluster strategy and coordinate fisheries management plans.

column7: Responsible investment promotion and skills training
column12: The project finances commercial viability assessments, investment promotion activities and skills training/technical assistance to attract responsible investors to the seafood cluster.

column7: Improve landing infrastructure and export of fresh fish
column12: The project supports better organization and management of the commercial port, artisanal/coastal fishing port, and airport, including financing a refrigerated warehouse at the airport and trade facilitation to promote export of fresh fish.

column7: Capacity building for small‑scale fishers and women
column12: The project will train small‑scale fishers, vulnerable groups and local suppliers—including women—in management and investment practices, and provide technical assistance on product quality, environmental management, eco‑certification and good fishing practices to reduce post‑harvest losses.

column7: Increased investments and fresh fish exports
column12: Results indicators include total investments generated from responsible investors and the volume of fresh fish export as measures of success for the seafood cluster.

column7: Training and inclusivity outcomes
column12: The results framework tracks direct project beneficiaries, percentage of female beneficiaries, number of training days (total and for women), and satisfaction among tripartite stakeholders.

column7: Policy and institutional reforms for fisheries management
column12: Indicators measure adoption of strategic cluster framework documents, completion of commercial viability studies and adoption of a PPP policy framework to support sustainable fisheries management.

column7: Support green and resilient growth through fiscal sustainability and green reforms
column12: The Program aims to strengthen resilient, private sector‑led growth through fiscal sustainability and enhanced access to finance and markets, and foster green growth with a focus on renewable natural resources.

column7: Reforms for fiscal sustainability, access to finance and green growth
column12: Reforms include revising external commercial borrowing, adopting digital payments and e‑commerce licensing with a focus on women, adopting the Food and Nutrition Security Policy and Biodiversity Act, implementing carbon market rules under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, improving customs rules and reducing import tariffs, and enhancing agricultural exports and renewable natural resources.

column7: Improved financial stability and access to credit
column12: Key results include resolution of non‑performing loans, improved access to finance, and greater transparency of fiscal risks.

column7: Gender‑inclusive digital and e‑commerce participation
column12: Results indicators include the number of e‑commerce business licenses, including those issued to women, and the volume of digital payments as measures of improved access to digital markets.

column7: Enhanced environmental sustainability and green growth
column12: Key results track adoption of the Food and Nutrition Security Policy and Biodiversity Act, operationalization of carbon markets, increased export value of agricultural products, share of women in farmer groups/cooperatives, number of proposals accessing genetic resources, and emission offsets generated from hydropower and renewable resources.

column7: Improve livestock livelihoods and strengthen animal health services
column12: PDO: The Project Development Objective is to sustainably improve livestock‑based livelihoods and strengthen animal health services in target project locations.

column7: Climate‑smart technology packages and producer organization support
column12: Sub‑component 1.1 will finance climate‑smart technology and practice packages such as improved breed, feed and fodder production, rangeland management, good animal husbandry practices, manure management, crop‑livestock integration and climate‑smart water and feeding equipment, and will strengthen producer groups through technical assistance and link them to agribusinesses.

column7: Market access and value chain infrastructure upgrades
column12: Sub‑component 1.2 promotes smallholder market access by establishing business partnerships and improving post‑harvest infrastructure—including slaughterhouses, market facilities and processing units—to facilitate processing and trade of livestock products, with technical assistance for smallholders to participate in value chains.

column7: Demonstration farms, extension services and disease surveillance
column12: Sub‑component 2.1 supports demonstration farms and IEC‑based extension programs to train farmers and encourage adoption of technologies, while Sub‑component 2.2 strengthens veterinary service delivery and disease surveillance by enhancing workforce skills, incentives and surveillance and response capacities.

column7: Increased sales of livestock products and adoption of climate‑smart technologies
column12: Result indicators include the percentage increase in volume of gross sales of livestock and products and the number of farmers adopting climate‑smart technologies and practices.

column7: Improved satisfaction with animal health services
column12: A key result indicator tracks the percentage of farmers satisfied with animal health services, reflecting improvements in veterinary service delivery and surveillance.

column7: Gender-inclusive beneficiary reach
column12: The project anticipates 30,000 direct beneficiaries, of whom 40 percent are women; about 20,000 farmers will benefit from training, co‑financing for technologies and improved infrastructure and services.

column7: Enhance dairy productivity and income resilience for cattle farmers
column12: The new Project Development Objective is to enhance dairy animal productivity and promote income generating and COVID‑19 resilience building activities for dairy cattle farmers in selected regions of the Kyrgyz Republic.

column7: Quality platform expansion and climate‑resilient dairy infrastructure
column12: Sub‑component 1A will expand financing to an additional 25 Jamaats and 260 collection points for small‑scale climate‑resilient dairy storage infrastructure and equipment, including purchase of milk collection and cooling equipment, energy‑efficient infrastructure and milk testing tools.

column7: Enhanced veterinary diagnostics and breeding services
column12: Sub‑component 1B provides additional technical assistance and critical equipment for veterinary laboratories in Karakol and Balykchy and capacity‑building for laboratories in Naryn and Talas. Sub‑component 1C focuses on artificial insemination by financing importation of improved genetic material and delivery of AI services and supporting the State Breeding Station’s performance reporting system.

column7: Strengthen milk processors and market access
column12: Sub‑component 1D provides financing to about 10–12 milk processors to develop new processed products, diversify product lines, adopt climate‑ and nutrition‑smart technologies, improve market information systems, comply with food safety requirements and implement worker health and safety measures.

column7: Training and demonstration farms for farmer groups
column12: Sub‑component 2A continues training and capacity building for about 400 new farmer groups, with special measures for returned migrants. Sub‑component 2B scales up demonstration farms that provide modern dairy equipment and climate‑resilient shelters. Sub‑component 2C establishes community seed funds to procure high‑quality fodder seeds and fertilizer and provides training and technical assistance for quality fodder production.

column7: Micro‑loans and farm‑level investments for dairy production
column12: The revolving fund provides micro‑loans for productive investments, including purchase of high‑quality animals, improved animal housing, manure management, drought‑resistant feed production, milk cooling and storage, and other investments to increase productivity; loans have terms of up to ten months for working capital and up to three years for longer‑term investments.

column7: Increases in milk yield and household income
column12: The project targets raising the average lactation period milk yield per cow at least 10 percent and increasing farm household income from milk sales by at least 10 percent.

column7: Farmers adopting improved livestock practices
column12: The project aims for at least 8,000 farm households to adopt improved animal feeding, health, breeding and management practices.

column7: Expanded access to finance and productive assets
column12: The project will expand the revolving fund to extend micro‑loans to additional beneficiaries, allowing them to purchase high‑quality animals, improved housing, manure management systems, drought‑resistant feed production and milk cooling and storage equipment.

column7: Increase productivity and climate resilience of selected agri‑food clusters
column12: The PDO is to increase productivity and climate resilience of selected agri‑food clusters and, in case of an eligible crisis or emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

column7: Investment loans for dairy and horticulture clusters

column7: Horticulture cluster investments and sustainable practices

column7: Modernization of seed systems
column12: The seed system improvement sub‑component supports review of policies and regulatory frameworks, development and multiplication of improved climate‑resilient seed varieties, modernization of laboratories and testing centers, and training of seed producers for multiplication of high‑quality seeds and planting materials.

column7: Improved livestock breeding and information management system
column12: The sub‑component supports development of animal breeding policies and a national breeding plan, provides quality bulls and climate‑smart technologies to breeding farms, upgrades regional veterinary laboratories, establishes a breeding information system, expands AI technicians and integrates a One Health approach.

column7: Operational support, project management and gender activities

column7: Increased yields and sales in agri‑food clusters

column7: Strengthen pandemic preparedness and response and improve basic health services
column12: The Project Development Objective is to strengthen cross‑sectoral capacity for pandemic preparedness and response and improve basic health services and quality of care.

column7: Conduct One Health capacity assessments and develop emergency procedures
column12: The project will conduct assessments to implement a One Health approach, including analyzing the organization of ministries responsible for One Health, evaluating existing information systems and their interoperability, developing procedural manuals for emergency resource distribution, and health risk communication strategies.

column7: Establish cross‑sectoral coordination platform and rapid response centers
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 aims to improve cross‑sectoral coordination and collaboration by setting up an operational coordination platform for One Health, delivering joint training in the International Health Regulations for human, animal and environmental health staff, establishing regional and district rapid response centres and strengthening logistical capacity for emergency response (stockpiles and treatment centres).

column7: Strengthen disease surveillance and reporting systems
column12: The project will strengthen human and animal disease surveillance systems by developing harmonized surveillance and reporting procedures, harmonizing electronic surveillance systems to ensure interoperability, expanding surveillance of antimicrobial resistance, increasing sentinel sites, piloting digital surveillance technologies and improving community‑level surveillance for both human and animal health.

column7: Improve quality and capacity of human and animal health laboratories
column12: Subcomponent 1.4 will strengthen laboratory quality through mapping and strengthening human and animal health laboratories, establishing laboratory quality standards, purchasing specialized equipment, creating a Laboratory Information Management System linking human, animal and environmental health laboratories, and improving data management and biosafety.

column7: One Health platform established and functional
column12: The results framework includes an indicator on establishing a functional One Health platform for cross‑sectoral coordination and pandemic preparedness.

column7: Interoperable electronic notification system operational
column12: The results framework specifies establishment of an interoperable electronic notification system across human, animal and environmental health sectors for disease surveillance and reporting.

column7: Improved laboratory quality for human and animal health
column12: PDO‑level indicators track progress in improving laboratory quality through capacity levels ranging from “No capacity” to “Sustainable” for human and animal health laboratories.

column12: The project aims to improve the productivity of smallholder farmers and market access of selected commodities in selected districts.

column7: Pilot livestock pass‑on program for smallholders
column12: A new subcomponent introduces livestock production and productivity by promoting a market‑oriented pilot pass‑on program in which farmers receive livestock and pass offspring to other households, with strategic planning led by the Department of Animal Health and Livestock Development.

column7: Increased productivity of targeted smallholder farmers
column12: Key results include increased yield of maize, rice and groundnuts, the number of marketing centres connected by upgraded roads, and adoption of improved agricultural technology among smallholder farmers.

column7: Enhance productivity and commercialization of non‑pastoral animal production and strengthen crisis response
column12: The project aims to enhance productivity and commercialization of non‑pastoral animal production in selected value chains and strengthen Mali’s capacity to respond to crises or emergencies.

column7: Improve genetics, feed and husbandry practices

column7: Develop sector policies and regulatory frameworks
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 will assist in formulating sector policies, breeding policies and regulatory frameworks to reduce pollution and guide development of the livestock sector.

column7: Strengthen livestock value chains and market infrastructure
column12: Component 2 will strengthen competitiveness by organizing markets and incentive frameworks, building capacity of producer associations, and constructing or rehabilitating infrastructure such as livestock markets, culling platforms and milk collection centres.

column12: Subcomponent 2.3 will provide matching grants and credit for about 160 Productive Partnerships and 600 microprojects to finance investments in livestock value chains, including support to business plan preparation and coordination with financial institutions.

column7: Establish crisis prevention and management mechanisms
column12: Component 3 includes establishing a Crisis Prevention and Management Unit, developing crisis response tools and early warning systems, supporting a contingent emergency response component and providing institutional support and data for the livestock sector.

column7: Provide training and capacity building for ABP management

column7: Enhanced competitiveness of livestock producers

column7: Improve performance of small producers and AgriMSMEs and natural resource management

column7: Provide nutrition training and mobile kitchens
column12: Subcomponent 5.3 includes training women on the use of local products for nutrition and deploying mobile kitchens to demonstrate food preparation and nutrition.

column7: Increased resilience and income for small farmers, breeders and fishermen
column12: By supplying inputs, livestock infrastructure, goats and aquaculture support, the project aims to strengthen resilience and income earning capacity of small farmers, breeders and fishermen.

column7: Improved veterinary diagnostic capacity

column7: Improve livelihoods and economic opportunities

column7: Improved access to climate‑resilient services and livelihoods

column7: Youth participation in livelihood opportunities

column12: The project expects beneficiaries to transform subsistence farming into climate‑ and nutrition‑smart systems, increasing food production and income from selling surpluses.

column7: Enhanced resilience and climate‑smart agriculture adoption
column12: Agri‑food innovation plans will train farmers to adopt climate‑ and nutrition‑smart agriculture, improving resilience to future disasters and climatic risks.

column7: Inclusivity through targeting women, youth and persons with disabilities

column12: Subcomponent 1.3 will strengthen policy and legal frameworks, develop crisis response tools and early warning systems, conduct climate risk analysis and integrate gender considerations.

column12: Subcomponent 2.2 introduces a cost‑sharing financing program with two windows (one for general farmers/SMEs and another targeting vulnerable regions, women and youth), offering matching grants and a risk‑sharing facility to guarantee loans.

column7: Provide risk‑sharing facility and technical assistance to financial institutions
column12: The risk‑sharing facility provides partial credit guarantees and technical assistance to financial institutions to encourage lending to agri‑food SMEs and producers and improve risk assessment and portfolio management.

column7: Increased yield of livestock products (cattle meat and eggs)
column12: PDO indicators include the percentage increase in yields of livestock products such as cattle meat and eggs.

column7: Increase in value of marketed agricultural commodities
column12: PDO‑level outcomes measure increases in the value of marketed agricultural commodities produced by small and medium farmers and agri‑food SMEs.

column7: Farmers reached with agricultural assets or services (women and youth)
column12: PDO indicators track the number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services, disaggregated by gender and youth.

column7: Policies developed and revised
column12: Intermediate results indicators count the number of sectoral policies developed or revised as part of the project.

column7: Farmers satisfied with extension and veterinary services
column12: Intermediate results indicators measure the percentage of farmers satisfied with the extension and veterinary services provided by the project.

column7: Reduced time to deliver crisis support
column12: Indicators measure the average time needed to reach 80 percent of beneficiaries during crises, reflecting improved crisis response.

column7: Matching grant accounts opened and loans disbursed
column12: Results indicators track the number of matching grant accounts opened and the volume of loans disbursed under the cost‑sharing financing program, including repayment performance.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PID datasheet states that the project development objective (PDO) is to improve the resilience of the populations and of production systems to climate change and variability in targeted communes.

column7: Mainstream climate resilience into sector policies and local development plans
column12: The project’s Component 1 aims to make socioeconomic development policies more responsive to climate change and to implement a communication strategy and knowledge management system. Sub‑component 1.1 supported integrating climate change into national sector strategies and local development plans so that policies in health, water and roads account for climate impacts, and the Additional Financing will provide technical assistance to translate these strategies into action plans and align Niger’s policies with its Nationally Determined Contribution.

column7: Communication strategy and knowledge management with new technologies
column12: The project’s sub‑component 1.2 provided technical assistance, goods and services for defining and implementing a communication strategy and an effective knowledge management system. The AF introduces sub‑component 1.3 to integrate new technologies, such as satellite imagery, into the knowledge management system and improve spatial planning and disaster‑risk management, linking with the project’s monitoring tools.

column7: Improve resilience of agro‑sylvo‑pastoral systems and scale up sustainable land management
column12: Intermediate indicators for Component 2 include the percentage of producers adopting SLM practices introduced by the project and the number of agricultural and sylvo‑pastoral hectares under SLM. The project also measures the quantity of animal feed supplements produced and the number of integrated services platforms ("Maisons du paysan") that provide advisory services and storage for feed and inputs.

column7: Adaptive social protection and support for vulnerable households
column12: The project description notes that a new sub‑component integrates innovative measures for protecting the most poor and vulnerable households. Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) activities will be financed to help households cope with climate shocks and variability.

column7: Integrated services platforms ("Maisons du paysan")
column12: Intermediate indicators count the number of operational integrated services platforms known as “Maisons du paysan.” These platforms provide advisory services, storage facilities and training to support agricultural and pastoral producers and improve climate resilience.

column7: Policies incorporating climate resilience
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of sector policies incorporating climate resilience and the number of local development plans and annual investment plans that integrate climate resilience.

column7: Dissemination of climate resilience knowledge products
column12: The project aims to disseminate 60 climate resilience knowledge products and inform 2 million people about climate issues.

column7: Producers adopting sustainable land management practices
column12: Component 2 indicators measure the percentage of producers adopting SLM practices introduced by the project, along with additional agricultural and sylvo‑pastoral areas brought under SLM.

column7: Animal feed supplements produced
column12: The project tracks the quantity of animal food supplements produced (40,000 tons per year) as an indicator of enhanced fodder and feed availability.

column7: Operational integrated services platforms
column12: Intermediate indicators record the number of operational integrated services platforms (“Maisons du paysan”) established by the project.

column7: Community facilities protected or rehabilitated
column12: Indicators include the number of community facilities that have been protected, restored or rehabilitated, reflecting enhanced resilience to climate shocks.

column7: Households benefiting from adaptive social protection
column12: The project records the number of households benefiting from accumulated ASP activities as an intermediate indicator.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PID notes that the project development objective is to increase agriculture productivity and access to markets for small and medium farmers and agri‑food SMEs in the participating project regions, and to provide immediate and effective response to an eligible crisis or emergency.

column7: Improve agricultural support services and policies
column12: The PID states that the additional financing will replenish component 1 of the Agriculture and Livestock Transformation Project, which supports agricultural support services and policies, including capacity building for institutions and farmers.

column7: Investments in agricultural production, processing and market access
column12: The PID lists Component 2 as increasing investments in agricultural production, processing and market access, indicating that the project continues to invest in these areas to support farmers and agri‑food SMEs.

column7: Contingent emergency response for flood recovery
column12: The PID explains that the additional financing replenishes funds because the Contingent Emergency Response Component was activated following unprecedented floods in 2020. Results indicators include the percentage of people protected by water management infrastructure, number of emergency kits distributed, drinking water wells rehabilitated and length of dyke and riverbank rehabilitation.

column7: People protected by water management infrastructure
column12: The revised results framework measures the percentage of people harmed by floods who are protected and served by water management infrastructure.

column7: Emergency kits distributed
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of emergency kits distributed as part of the project’s Contingent Emergency Response Component.

column7: Drinking water wells rehabilitated
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of drinking water wells rehabilitated under the emergency response component.

column7: Dyke and riverbank rehabilitation
column12: The results framework measures the length of dyke and riverbank rehabilitation as part of flood recovery efforts.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PAD states that the project development objective is to increase the adoption of climate‑smart landscape restoration practices and improve access to income earning opportunities in targeted communes in Niger.

column7: National inventory and management plans for forests, pastoral lands and fisheries
column12: Component 1 focuses on knowledge creation and territorial planning, including preparing Niger’s first national forest and pastoral lands inventory, developing management plans for forests, pastoral areas and fisheries, and supporting climate‑informed territorial planning with integrated landscape and communal development plans and an MRV system.

column7: Landscape restoration: natural regeneration, reforestation, dune‑fixing and hedges
column12: The project’s investment component restores landscapes through natural regeneration, dune‑fixing, reforestation, establishing hedges and multipurpose plantations, and restoring degraded pastoral and agro‑silvo‑pastoral lands. It also develops pastoral enclaves and corridors and distributes improved stoves and renewable energy systems.

column7: Integrated community agro‑silvo‑pastoral farms and matching grants for local livelihoods
column11: cattle; small ruminants; poultry; fish; bees
column12: Sub‑component 2.2 provides matching grants to promote sustainable development of non‑timber forest products and artisanal fishery products and to preserve cultural heritage. It also finances integrated community agro‑silvo‑pastoral farms (FACI), which include processing units, storage, advisory services and training, as well as facilities for forestry, beekeeping, fish farming, horticulture and small livestock production, targeting women and youth.

column7: Project coordination, monitoring and conflict management
column12: Component 3 covers project coordination, monitoring and evaluation, development of communication tools, and promotion of conflict reduction strategies to support landscape restoration and improve social cohesion.

column7: Land area under sustainable landscape management
column12: PDO‑level indicators include land area under sustainable landscape management practices (a corporate results indicator).

column7: Producer organizations with increased access to income opportunities
column12: PDO‑level indicators include the number of producer organizations with increased access to income opportunities.

column7: Net greenhouse gas emissions
column12: PDO‑level indicators include net greenhouse gas emissions (metric tons of CO₂ per year).

column7: Areas under management plans and inventories
column12: The results framework tracks the area under management plans for forests, pastoral areas and fisheries, and the completion of the national forest and pastoral lands inventory.

column7: Women‑led organizations receiving grants and businesses registered
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of women‑led organizations receiving grants and the number of women‑led businesses registered, reflecting efforts to empower women economically.

column7: Integrated community farms operational
column11: cattle; small ruminants; poultry; fish; bees
column12: The results framework includes the number of integrated community farms (FACIs) that are operational, capturing progress in establishing diversified livelihood enterprises.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PAD states that the project development objective is to increase productivity, commercialization and climate resilience for project beneficiaries.

column7: Improve crop productivity through improved seeds and advisory services
column12: The project will scale up e‑voucher systems so farmers can access improved certified seeds with climate‑smart characteristics, provide advisory services on seed selection and use, and strengthen seed quality control and certification. It also promotes private sector participation in seed production and distribution and supports the national seed committee.

column7: Develop irrigation using renewable energy and efficient technologies
column12: The project finances 9,900 ha of small‑scale irrigation and 8,200 ha of medium and large‑scale irrigation, focusing on renewable energy and efficient water conveyance. It also develops a price reference system for irrigation materials, conducts feasibility studies and provides training and support to farmers’ organizations.

column7: Strengthen farmer organizations and provide digital advisory services
column12: The PAD notes that the project will organize and strengthen farmer organizations, provide training on climate‑smart agricultural practices and postharvest management, and promote digital technologies and extension services to enhance productivity.

column7: Genetic improvement and animal husbandry support
column12: The project supports building and equipping artificial insemination and breed improvement centers, training technical staff, providing AI services, and distributing high‑performance male sheep and goats. It promotes production of improved fodder and feed preservation techniques, rehabilitates and constructs water points, trains farmers on animal housing, feeding and hygiene, and strengthens poultry disease surveillance.

column7: Applied agricultural research and AgTech development
column12: The project funds multiplication of climate‑smart seeds, testing of germplasm, development of crop management practices to enhance water use efficiency and soil quality, and creation of AgTech applications and services including remote sensing tools and communication links between research and farmers.

column7: Climate‑resilient market infrastructure and processing facilities
column12: The project will construct cool, dry and ventilated storage facilities, energy‑efficient warehouses and processing equipment; establish standards for onion sorting, storage and packaging; build energy‑efficient rice mills operated by cooperatives; and finance milk collection and cooling centers and completion of an abattoir. It will also train actors in health standards.

column7: Strengthen food safety, sanitary and phytosanitary capacity
column12: The project will strengthen the General Directorate for Plant Protection and Veterinary Services to conduct sanitary inspections, disease surveillance and monitoring of pesticide and drug residues. Capacity strengthening includes training and awareness raising on climate risk, animal health and food safety.

column7: Mobilize private investors and promote industry dialogue
column12: The project will map transformative private investors and land areas for investment, conduct prefeasibility studies, establish industry dialogue platforms to facilitate interactions between producers and value chain actors, encourage partnerships and contract farming, and support development and dissemination of quality standards.

column7: Access to finance through credit enhancement and guarantees
column12: The PAD notes that the project will provide credit enhancement grants and guarantees for commercial loans via FISAN and SAHFI, support financial institutions to develop agriculture‑appropriate financial products, and promote warehouse receipt financing.

column7: Area with new or improved irrigation
column12: PDO indicators include the area provided with new or improved irrigation or drainage services.

column7: Increased yield of targeted agricultural products
column12: The PDO‑level indicator measures the percentage increase in yield of targeted agriculture products among targeted beneficiaries.

column7: Increased yield of selected animal products
column12: PDO indicators include the percentage increase in yield of selected animal products among targeted beneficiaries (e.g., increased weight of cattle for red meat production).

column7: Increased volume of crop products sold
column12: The PDO indicators include the increased volume of targeted crop value chains sold by beneficiary households.

column7: Increased volume of livestock products sold
column12: PDO indicators measure the increased volume of targeted livestock products sold by beneficiary households.

column7: People with enhanced resilience to climate risks
column12: PDO indicators include the number of people with enhanced resilience to climate risks and the share of women among them.

column7: People with strengthened food and nutrition security
column12: The PDO includes the number of people with strengthened food and nutrition security as a corporate scorecard indicator.

column7: Farmers reached with agricultural assets or services
column12: The results framework lists the number of farmers reached with agricultural assets or services as an intermediate indicator.

column7: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices
column12: Intermediate indicators include the land area under sustainable landscape management practices.

column7: Farmers adopting good animal husbandry practices
column12: Intermediate indicators track the number of farmers adopting good animal husbandry practices introduced by the project.

column7: Market infrastructure built or rehabilitated
column12: The results framework includes the number of market infrastructures built or rehabilitated, with breakdowns for warehouses and temporary storage facilities for rice, cowpeas and onions.

column7: Livestock market infrastructure built or rehabilitated
column12: Intermediate indicators report the number of livestock markets, milk collection centers and slaughterhouses built or rehabilitated by the project.

column7: Farmer and herder cooperatives linked to markets
column12: The project’s intermediate indicators include the number of farmer and herder cooperatives linked to markets.

column7: Women‑led firms with access to agriculture finance
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of women‑led firms with increased access to agriculture finance, reflecting efforts to reduce gender gaps.

column7: Sub‑projects financed and loans leveraged
column12: Intermediate indicators report the number of sub‑projects financed and the amount of loans extended to the agriculture sector through the project’s credit enhancement grants and guarantees.

column7: Program Development Objective
column12: The PAD states that the Program Development Objective is to enhance productivity and market access of priority commodity value chains and livestock in the Extended Groundnut Basin and agro‑pastoral areas.

column7: Strengthen seed systems and smart subsidies
column12: The PAD describes results area 1 interventions that strengthen seed systems and implement digital smart subsidies for seeds, fertilizer and mechanization, coupled with advisory services to increase crop productivity.

column7: Climate risk management and small‑scale water infrastructure
column12: The PAD notes that climate risk management measures include small‑scale water infrastructure for integrated rainfed crop–livestock production, adoption of climate‑smart practices, integrated soil fertility and water management, and diversification of crop and livestock systems.

column7: Improve animal health, genetics and feed
column12: The PAD lists livestock interventions such as implementing the PPR eradication strategy, vaccinating against Newcastle disease and fowlpox, updating the Animal Health Code, increasing forage production, improving dairy genetics, introducing improved housing and herd management practices and strengthening veterinary services.

column7: Diversification and high‑value crops with small irrigation
column12: Results area 1 includes diversification into tree crops and horticulture, supported by small‑scale water retention and irrigation. It also mentions a cash transfer program to support vulnerable households.

column7: Groundnut sector reforms and value chain governance
column12: The PAD details reforms in the groundnut sector: revising groundnut regulation and pricing systems, liberalizing marketing, restructuring the inter‑profession, improving aflatoxin control and quality management, and promoting contract farming.

column7: Invest in market infrastructure and logistics
column12: Results area 2 focuses on market access, including investments in storage and processing facilities, feeder roads, milk collection centers, livestock markets and value chain logistics. It also promotes private investment, agricultural insurance and a warehouse receipt system.

column7: Strengthen sector governance and advisory bodies
column12: Results area 3 supports implementation of LOASP and CSOASP, establishment of regional agro‑sylvo‑pastoral committees (CRASPs), strengthening agricultural statistics and sector data, and improving agricultural extension and advisory services.

column7: Yield increase of groundnut
column12: PDO indicators include the yield increase of groundnuts as a measure of enhanced productivity.

column7: Increase in shelled groundnut exports
column12: PDO indicators measure the increase in exports of shelled groundnuts.

column7: Decrease in mortality of small ruminants
column12: PDO indicators include a decrease in the mortality rate of small ruminants, reflecting improved animal health.

column7: Increase in dairy farming productivity
column12: PDO indicators include an increase in dairy farming productivity.

column7: Increase in volume of milk commercialized
column12: PDO indicators include an increase in the volume of milk commercialized as a measure of improved market access.

column7: Farmers reached with agricultural assets and services
column12: PDO indicators include the number of farmers reached with agricultural assets and services.

column7: Program Development Objective
column12: The PID states that the project development objective is to enhance productivity and market access of priority commodity value chains and livestock in the extended groundnut basin and agro‑pastoral areas.

column7: Integrated crop and livestock development with climate‑smart practices
column12: The PID notes that the program pursues integrated crop–livestock development, climate‑smart practices, diversification, irrigation development, improved seeds and advisory services.

column7: Yield increase of groundnut
column12: The PID lists the yield increase of groundnuts as a results indicator.

column7: Increase in production of selected livestock products
column12: The PID indicates that one of the results indicators is the increase in production of selected livestock products.

column7: Increase in exports of high‑value crops
column12: The PID specifies that an indicator is the increase in exports of high‑value crops.

column7: Farmers and herders reached with assets and services
column12: The PID lists the number of farmers and herders reached with agricultural assets and services as a results indicator.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PAD states that the project development objective is to increase investment in three target protected area landscapes to grow the biodiversity economy and benefits to local communities.

column7: Multi‑stakeholder coordination and master planning
column12: The PAD explains that sub‑component 1.1 will bring stakeholders together to develop a shared vision for biodiversity economy nodes, coordinate actions, conduct feasibility studies and integrate master plans into municipal and spatial planning to align investments.

column7: SMME support and mentorship
column12: The project supports SMMEs by offering training, mentorship, and small grants to help them start or expand operations, emphasizing support for women‑led businesses and job opportunities for women and youth.

column7: Strengthen governance and community benefit sharing
column12: The PAD notes that sub‑component 1.3 will strengthen governance capacity and ownership models to ensure equitable benefit sharing through community equity ownership and leadership training with a focus on women.

column7: Community stewardship and expansion of protected areas
column12: The project will support community stewardship agreements to expand wildlife habitat, provide technical assistance for land management and restoration and develop capacity through training youth community monitors.

column7: Knowledge exchange and replication
column12: Component 2 will capture lessons from the project sites and facilitate knowledge exchange across biodiversity economy nodes and within regional and global forums to replicate successful approaches.

column7: Land area under improved practices
column12: PDO outcome indicators include the area of landscapes under improved practices measured in hectares.

column7: Public and private resources leveraged
column12: PDO indicators include the volume of public and private sector resources leveraged for the wildlife sector.

column7: SMME businesses supported
column12: PDO indicators include the number of SMME businesses in biodiversity economy nodes supported to start or expand operations.

column7: Beneficiaries disaggregated by gender
column12: PDO indicators include the number of beneficiaries, disaggregated by gender, benefitting from biodiversity economy interventions.

column7: Hectares assessed as potential expansion land
column12: The results framework includes an intermediate indicator for hectares assessed as potential expansion land in the project nodes.

column7: Micro business operators reached and female share
column12: The results framework measures micro‑business operators reached and the proportion of beneficiaries who are women.

column7: Community governance members trained
column12: Intermediate indicators record the number of community governance members (including women) who receive leadership training.

column7: Stakeholders participating in consultations
column12: The results framework tracks the number of stakeholders participating in consultation processes and the percentage of grievances resolved within the required timeframe.

column7: Community satisfaction with project results
column12: An indicator measures the percentage of targeted community members satisfied with project results.

column7: Project Development Objective
column12: The PAD states that the objective of the project is to increase black rhino populations in target protected areas in South Africa.

column7: Expand habitat and improve water and security infrastructure at Addo Elephant National Park
column12: The PAD describes investments at Addo Elephant National Park, including translocating rhinos to expand their habitat, constructing boreholes and water points, fencing new sections, upgrading rhino bomas and enhancing security through control rooms, fences, access control, vehicles, communications equipment and training.

column7: Secure and manage rhino populations at Great Fish River Nature Reserve
column12: The project will relocate rhinos within the Great Fish River Nature Reserve, improve water management through water points and dam removal, maintain infrastructure and strengthen security with control rooms, communication networks, fences and training of security staff.

column7: National and regional enabling conditions for rhino conservation
column12: The PAD notes that Component 2 strengthens national and regional enabling conditions by coordinating security and research, integrating work plans and budgets, hiring a law enforcement advisor, sharing lessons and conducting research to achieve rhino population growth.

column7: Increase in black rhino populations (CAGR)
column12: PDO‑level indicators include the percent increase of black rhino populations in the target sites (compound annual growth rate).

column7: Area under improved management
column12: The results framework measures the area under improved management by site as an indicator of enhanced conservation management.

column7: Beneficiaries of conservation services
column12: The results framework includes the number of direct and indirect beneficiaries of conservation services, disaggregated by gender.

column7: Rhino mortality rate
column12: Intermediate indicators include the annual mortality rate of rhinos, reflecting improved protection.

column7: Rangers per square kilometre
column12: The results framework records the number of rangers per square kilometre as an indicator of security and management capacity.

column7: Reinforce capacity of Ministry of Agriculture and increase market access, improve livelihoods and enable emergency response
column12: The proposed development objective is to reinforce the capacity of the Ministry of Agriculture, Natural Resources and Rural Development to provide or facilitate access to services in the agricultural sector; increase market access to small producers and food security in selected areas; improve livelihood in areas affected by Hurricane Matthew; and enable the Government to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible emergency.

column7: Scale up voucher schemes and matching grants for agricultural inputs
column12: The existing voucher schemes and matching grants will be scaled up to reach 7,000 additional beneficiaries in the selected areas.

column7: Animal husbandry support with training, forage, enclosures and beekeeping
column12: The new Animal Husbandry subcomponent will support about 6,000 households, providing training, forage production, construction of goat enclosures, and provision of beehives and protective equipment for beekeeping.

column7: Irrigation rehabilitation and micro‑catchment protection
column12: The Irrigation Rehabilitation and micro‑catchment protection subcomponent will rehabilitate small-scale canals, river embankments, drains, and protect micro catchments through cash-for-work civil works.

column7: Households supported and female beneficiaries
column12: The project will support 41,000 Hurricane Matthew-affected households and increase total beneficiaries to 60,000, with at least 40% women.

column7: Rehabilitation of irrigation area and restocking of animals
column12: Emergency assistance will rehabilitate irrigation infrastructure across 3,500 hectares and restock small animals for approximately 6,000 poor households.

column7: Promote socio-economic productive activities to improve livelihoods of Miskito indigenous peoples
column12: The project development objective is to promote socio-economic productive activities to improve the livelihoods of Miskito indigenous peoples in selected territories.

column7: Matching grants for mixed agriculture, poultry and fishery activities
column12: Component 1 provides matching grants to finance community-level subprojects promoting productive activities such as mixed agriculture (beans, rice, tomatoes), poultry farming and artisanal fishing equipment, with training and technical assistance.

column7: Community consultation and capacity building
column12: Component 2 focuses on consultation, participation and outreach, providing continuous training and technical assistance to empower communities under a community-driven development approach.

column7: Increased income and reduced production costs for beneficiaries
column12: Key results indicators target increasing income for 60% of beneficiaries by 20% and reducing production costs for 60% of beneficiaries by 20%.

column7: Increased productivity and number of beneficiaries adopting technologies
column12: The project aims for 60% of beneficiaries to increase productivity and tracks adoption of lower-cost technologies and implementation of business plans, with a target of 900 direct beneficiaries (40% women).

column7: Enhance productivity and climate resilience of irrigated agriculture and improve water management and market opportunities
column12: The Project Development Objective is to enhance productivity and climate resilience of irrigated agriculture, improve water management, and increase market opportunities for farmers and agro-entrepreneurs in selected sub-basin areas of Tamil Nadu.

column7: Institutional strengthening for water resource management
column12: Subcomponent A.1 provides technical assistance to strengthen water resources institutions, including data collection, modern ICT tools, and establishment of an e-WRD app.

column7: Irrigation systems modernization and on-farm development
column12: Subcomponent A.2 rehabilitates and modernizes 4,800 tanks and 477 anicuts, improves water delivery, constructs on-farm development works and groundwater recharge structures.

column7: Participatory irrigation management through Water User Associations
column12: Subcomponent A.3 creates and supports 3,200 Water User Associations, provides training for operation and maintenance, and fosters participatory irrigation management.

column7: Climate-resilient crop production and diversification
column12: Subcomponent B.1 promotes climate-resilient and sustainable crop production systems by scaling resource-conservation technologies such as micro irrigation, System of Rice Intensification and System of Sugarcane Intensification, integrated soil fertility and pest management, and diversification into high-value crops.

column7: Livestock and inland fisheries improvement
column12: Subcomponent B.2 aims to improve dairy productivity through sustainable husbandry technologies, strengthen breeding programs and artificial insemination networks, expand fodder development and disease surveillance; it also modernizes inland fisheries with improved feed, fish seed, cage culture and value chain support.

column7: Agriculture marketing, value addition and FPO support
column12: Subcomponent B.3 supports the formation of commodity groups and Farmer Producer Organizations, builds post-harvest infrastructure, provides grants and training for marketing and value addition, and modernizes agricultural markets.

column7: Improved irrigation area and adoption of climate-resilient technologies
column12: PDO-level indicators track area with improved irrigation or drainage services, area under climate-resilient technologies, and increase in yields of rice, maize, pulses, vegetables and banana in selected sub-basin areas.

column7: Increased farmer income and market access
column12: Indicators include share of commodities sold through new marketing channels, number of project beneficiaries and female beneficiaries, reflecting improved market access and income.

column7: Improve upstream watershed management and increase agricultural water productivity in selected Gram Panchayats
column12: The Project Development Objective is to improve upstream watershed management and increase agricultural water productivity in selected Gram Panchayats in Himachal Pradesh.

column7: Sustainable land and water management practices
column12: Component 1 invests in soil and water conservation measures, reforestation, pasture management, improved seed stands and nurseries, forest fire prevention and research, and establishing community funds for operation and maintenance.

column7: Efficient irrigation and climate-smart agriculture practices
column12: Component 2 promotes efficient irrigation through drip and sprinkler systems, water harvesting and storage, and supports climate-smart agriculture practices including diversification into high-value crops, climate-resilient varieties, livestock-based activities for ruminants, and post-harvest interventions.

column7: Adoption of climate-smart practices and increased irrigation area
column12: PDO-level indicators include new farm area under higher efficiency irrigation, share of participating farmers adopting climate-smart agriculture practices (disaggregated by gender), and land area under sustainable landscape management.

column7: Institutional reforms and farmer satisfaction
column12: The project monitors the number of reforms implemented following institutional assessments and the share of participating farmers satisfied with interventions.

column7: Increase quality and coverage of animal health services and improve One Health coordination
column12: The Program Development Objective is to increase the quality and coverage of animal health services for livestock farmers and improve One Health coordination in participating states.

column7: Strengthen institutional capacity and One Health coordination
column12: Results Area 1 strengthens institutional capacity for integrated animal health management, establishes One Health platforms and training programs, and coordinates multi-sectoral actions.

column7: Improve access to veterinary services and disease control
column12: Results Area 2 increases access to quality animal health services via door-step delivery, trains veterinarians and veterinary workers, and strengthens disease surveillance and control programs.

column7: Upgrade diagnostic systems and digital disease surveillance
column12: The program supports upgrading animal health laboratories, expanding diagnostic capabilities, implementing a digital disease surveillance system, and training personnel to use the system.

column7: Promote adoption of good animal husbandry practices and biosecurity measures
column12: Results Area 5 aims to increase adoption of good animal husbandry practices and biosecurity by farmers through extension, training and demonstration of practices such as improved manure management and biogas usage.

column7: Achieve comprehensive vaccination coverage for nationally important animal diseases
column12: Results Area 6 seeks to achieve comprehensive vaccination coverage for nationally important animal diseases to improve animal health and productivity.

column7: Labs operating under quality assurance and farmers accessing improved services
column12: PDO-level indicators include the number of laboratories operating under improved quality assurance, the number of livestock farmers with increased access to improved animal health services (disaggregated by gender), and establishment of functional digital disease surveillance systems.

column7: One Health joint actions and adoption of biosecurity measures
column12: Indicators track the number of One Health joint actions implemented, the establishment of a state antimicrobial resistance (AMR) action plan, and the number of farmers adopting biosecurity measures.

column7: Improve landscape management and increase benefits for forest-dependent communities in Tripura and Nagaland
column12: The Project Development Objective is to improve landscape management and increase benefits for targeted forest-dependent communities in Tripura and Nagaland.

column7: Policy review and capacity building for integrated landscape management
column12: Component 1 develops climate-resilient landscape planning guidelines, conducts policy and regulatory reviews, and builds capacity of forest and land-use agencies through training and establishment of a forest-fire early warning system.

column7: R&D, value chain development and human-wildlife conflict management
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 upgrades research units, develops decision support systems, establishes a wildlife breeding centre for endangered species, and implements human–wildlife conflict management and management plans for conservation reserves.

column7: Strengthening community institutions and knowledge sharing
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 strengthens Joint Forest Management Committees, Biodiversity Management Committees and Self-Help Groups through gender-inclusive training; Subcomponent 1.4 creates a digital knowledge platform and organizes exchanges for information sharing.

column7: Community landscape restoration and livelihood diversification
column12: Component 2 finances community landscape management plans involving inventories, biodiversity conservation and water management, and funds restoration through soil and water conservation, fire management, climate-resilient agriculture and livelihood diversification such as micro-irrigation and vermicomposting.

column7: Development of value chains and ecotourism
column12: Component 3 develops agroforestry, forestry and non-timber forest product value chains, supports enterprises with matching grants and access to credit and PPPs, scales up honeybee rearing and value chain development, and promotes ecotourism and nature-based recreation.

column7: Areas under enhanced conservation and people benefitting from value chains
column12: PDO-level indicators include terrestrial and aquatic areas under enhanced conservation or management, net greenhouse gas emissions change in project landscapes, and number of people with increased benefits from landscape-based value chains and those with improved resilience to climate risks.

column7: Support development of environmentally sustainable, inclusive and competitive beef production
column12: The Program Development Objective is to support the development of an environmentally sustainable, inclusive, and competitive beef production in Kazakhstan.

column7: Unified animal recording and traceability system and veterinary services
column12: Results Area 1 establishes a unified animal recording and traceability system, integrating data across agencies, updating regulatory frameworks and building veterinary service capacity including reforms to enable private sector service delivery and control of major diseases.

column7: Farmer-centric extension services, matching grants and headage payments
column12: Results Area 2 scales up farmer-centric service delivery models by providing knowledge and extension services, training programs, model farms, matching grants to small and medium farmers and headage payments linked to feedlots, and improving access to land and pasture resources.

column7: Green growth policies and GHG MRV system
column12: Results Area 3 mainstreams green growth principles into state programs and establishes a greenhouse gas monitoring, reporting and verification system to guide adaptation and emissions reduction targets.

column7: Public expenditure on green growth and farmer participation

column7: Enhanced climate resilience and adaptation for farmers and livestock producers

column7: Uninterrupted access to bread and grain products for poor and vulnerable households

column7: Improved resilience of grain producers to climate change and water stress through adoption of climate‑resilient technologies and digitalized seed systems
column12: The project will improve resilience of grain producers by enhancing access to climate‑resilient technologies, digitalizing seed sector processes and improving knowledge of vulnerabilities and adaptation options.

column7: Increased animal productivity and reduced greenhouse gas emissions through improved feeding practices
column12: Advice to farmers on better feeding practices aims to increase animal productivity and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

column7: To help restore and promote job creation in the agri‑food sector in Tunisia
column12: The Project Development Objective is to help restore and promote job creation in the agri‑food sector in Tunisia.

column7: Provide technical assistance to producer organizations and SMEs for business development, project preparation, capacity building and resilience including digital and climate‑resilient practices

column7: Number of beneficiaries and direct and indirect jobs created

column7: Enhanced business resilience and economic inclusion for youth and women

column7: To strengthen capacity for sustainable and competitive agricultural growth and promote the use of climate‑smart agriculture in targeted regions in Turkey
column12: The Project Development Objective is to strengthen capacity for sustainable and competitive agricultural growth and promote the use of climate‑smart agriculture in targeted regions in Turkey.

column7: Establish a digital blueprint for agricultural data collection and forecasting, including yield and production models, integrated databases and training

column7: Establish a centralized Veterinary Medicinal Control Center and vaccine testing laboratories, including training and capacity building
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 establishes a centralized Veterinary Medicinal Control Center, constructs vaccine testing laboratories and provides training and capacity building to improve regulation and control of veterinary medicines and vaccines.

column7: Invest in climate‑resilient geothermal greenhouse clusters within specialized organized industrial zones
column12: Subcomponent 3.1 will pilot geothermal greenhouse clusters by investing in enabling infrastructure such as geothermal drilling, energy and water supply, establishing greenhouse infrastructure and mobilizing private sector investment in organized industrial zones.

column7: Promote adoption of climate‑smart agriculture technologies through awareness campaigns, digital technologies, matching grants and training
column12: Subcomponent 3.2 promotes adoption of climate‑smart agriculture technologies by conducting awareness and dissemination activities, providing digital tools and precision agriculture equipment, offering matching grants and conducting training and gender‑sensitive communication campaigns.

column7: Implement integrated manure management systems and pilot innovative manure collection, separation and processing for recycling to reduce water pollution and GHG emissions
column12: Subcomponent 3.3 will reduce animal production pressure on water pollution and GHG emissions by developing an integrated manure management system, establishing stakeholder networks, providing training and piloting innovative manure collection, separation and processing technologies for recycling into biofertilizers.

column7: Support research and innovations for climate‑smart agriculture, including integrated pest management, biofertilizers, energy‑saving technologies and gender‑inclusive research design
column12: Subcomponent 3.4 supports research and innovations for climate‑smart agriculture such as integrated pest management, alternative pest control methods, nutrient management, biofertilizers, energy‑saving technologies and gender‑inclusive research design and dissemination.

column7: Land area with integral information for sustainable and competitive agricultural land planning/management
column12: PDO indicators include the land area with integral information to develop sustainable and competitive agricultural land planning and management.

column7: Increase in analyses/tests for animal disease and zoonoses diagnostics processed in upgraded laboratories

column7: Number of farmers adopting climate‑smart agriculture technologies
column12: The results framework tracks the number of farmers adopting climate‑smart agricultural technologies, with an end target of 42,500 farmers.

column7: Area prepared for climate‑resilient greenhouse infrastructure
column12: Intermediate results indicators include the area prepared for climate‑resilient greenhouse infrastructure, with an end target of 179 ha.

column7: To support the resilient recovery of the agriculture sector in Türkiye’s earthquake‑affected provinces and targeted adjacent areas

column7: Implement Pasture Management Plans and procure goods and services for pasture restoration and digital pasture information systems, including solar panels, mobile shelters and seeds for degraded pastures

column7: Beneficiaries with recovered operating capacity

column7: Support competitive research grants and adaptive research to develop, validate and disseminate climate‑smart technologies and management practices (TIMPs)

column12: Subcomponent 1.3 will strengthen agro‑climate monitoring and information systems through acquisition and installation of weather stations, development of big data systems for agro‑climate information, partnerships to improve climate information dissemination and training extension staff for early warning and dissemination.

column7: Strengthen institutional capacity of research institutes and animal genetic resource centers by training staff, refurbishing laboratories, establishing mobile reproductive technology labs and upgrading veterinary labs

column12: Subcomponent 1.4 will strengthen institutional capacity by training extension and research staff, certifying and producing seeds, breeds and fingerlings, refurbishing laboratories and aquaculture facilities, establishing mobile artificial reproductive technology labs and upgrading veterinary laboratories.

column7: Provide matching grants and incentives for communities and districts to adopt sustainable land management practices, including micro‑projects and subprojects, mechanization and irrigation services and extension support

column12: Subcomponent 2.1 will finance matching grants for community‑level micro‑projects and district‑level subprojects to adopt sustainable land management practices, provide incentive payments through labor‑intensive public works and SLM payments to farmers, offer mechanization and irrigation services and deliver extension services.

column12: Subcomponent 2.2 will support refugee settlements and host communities by providing nutrition grants to farmer groups, scaling up backyard gardens for nutrient‑dense foods, contracting partners to deliver nutrition education, supplying climate‑smart inputs and micro‑irrigation kits and building capacity to manage savings and revolving funds.

column7: Build institutional capacity at local levels for CSA planning, farmer mobilization and climate adaptation education and deliver farmer field schools and extension
column12: Subcomponent 2.3 will build institutional capacity at district, subcounty and community levels for CSA planning, mobilize and organize farmer groups, strengthen extension services and provide education through farmer field schools and lead farmers, including consultations on climate change mitigation and adaptation.

column7: Provide technical assistance and matching grants for market development and linkages, including clean energy equipment, solar dryers, climate‑smart storage, market linkages and rehabilitation of market bottlenecks
column8: Markets & Finance; Food Processing & Storage; Advisory and Extension
column12: Subcomponent 3.1 will finance national technical assistance to strengthen producer organizations, business development services, matching grants for clean energy equipment and climate‑smart storage, promotion of market linkages and rehabilitation of market infrastructure bottlenecks.

column7: Provide training and matching grants for market development in refugee settlements and host communities, including clean energy equipment and value‑added processing
column8: Markets & Finance; Food Processing & Storage; Advisory and Extension
column12: Subcomponent 3.2 will finance skills development for youth and extension staff and provide matching grants for clean energy equipment, machinery and infrastructure for harvesting and postharvest value addition to minimize losses and improve quality.

column12: PDO indicators measure the land area under sustainable land management including climate‑smart practices resulting from project support.

column12: Intermediate results indicators include the number of farmers trained on the application of climate‑smart agriculture technologies and practices (with a target of 77,550, including 19,800 women) and extension staff/service providers trained.

column7: Increase use of productivity and nutrition-enhancing agricultural practices by smallholders
column12: To increase the use of productivity and nutrition-enhancing agricultural practices by smallholders in targeted project areas

column12: Investments under this subcomponent build on water harvesting and small-scale spate improvement … rehabilitation of existing or construction of new terraces; rehabilitation of on-farm water storage facilities … wadi soil conservation … vegetative measures; rehabilitation of shallow wells and springs

column7: Improve animal husbandry and veterinary services including vaccination and training
column12: Activities aim at protecting livestock assets of poor households through improving access to veterinary services … identification and training of Community Animal Health Workers … vaccination campaign to prevent major diseases in small ruminants, improving animal nutrition through demonstration of appropriate technologies … start-up packages for backyard poultry, small ruminants and apiculture

column7: Provide emergency livelihood kits and equipment for value addition and dairy value chain
column12: This subcomponent aims at improving livelihoods and nutrition and increasing value added … supporting vulnerable groups with provision of emergency agriculture livelihood kits … increasing value-added through provision of equipment and technical and business training for processing, packaging and marketing; improving honey quality through improved beekeeping and processing; supporting the dairy value chain by increasing efficiency and reducing cost of animal feed

column7: Capacity building and extension services including farmer field schools and nutrition awareness
column12: This component finances capacity building activities to strengthen skills of stakeholders … piloting and expanding Farmers Field Schools … topics linked to land and water management and livestock production, and promoting nutrition awareness targeted to women and households

column7: Households supported to resume crop and livestock production

column7: Households with strengthened land and water management
column12: Intermediate results indicators include the number of households with strengthened land and water management with a target of 18,000 households

column7: Increased milk production
column12: An intermediate result indicator measures increased milk production by project beneficiaries with a target of 10 percent increase

column7: Control desert locust outbreak, support livelihoods, and strengthen preparedness for future infestations
column12: The Project Development Objectives are to control the desert locust outbreak, support livelihoods in locust-affected areas and strengthen Yemen’s preparedness for future locust infestations.

column7: Establish continuous surveillance using satellite and field equipment with community training
column12: Activities will provide early warning of locust outbreaks through procurement of satellite maps and land surveillance equipment (elocust3, GPS, camping kits, 4WD pickups), and Training-of-Trainers sessions to ensure organized training for communities to participate in desert locust surveillance and monitoring.

column7: Implement locust control using bio-pesticides and equipment
column12: The control measures sub-component will reduce locust populations by neutralizing hopper bands using bio-pesticides and will procure 4WD pickup trucks, bio-pesticides, ULV sprayers, pumps, pesticide drum cleaners and protective equipment, with operational costs for control operations

column7: Monitor health risks and develop National Pest Management Strategy
column12: Risk reduction activities include procurement of Cholinesterase test systems, testing of human health and soil and water for contamination, preparation of a National Pest Management Strategy, and safety and awareness training for spraying teams

column7: Provide cash-for-work employment and women-focused activities in locust-affected areas
column12: The Cash for Work sub-component provides short-term employment to beneficiaries, primarily women, for activities such as clearing dead locusts, planting seedlings, rehabilitating water reservoirs, collecting locusts for fertilizer and feed, introducing pollinators, training women as community health workers, and encouraging home gardens and nutrition

column7: Restore livelihoods with productive asset kits and training on climate-smart crop and livestock practices
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 provides productive asset kits to affected households dependent on agriculture, livestock and beekeeping; trains producers to restart production based on climate-smart crop and livestock practices; supports climate-resilient grazing with legumes and grasses; and supplies emergency fodder and limited animal restocking

column7: Establish DLCC network and early warning system for locust outbreaks
column12: Component 3 builds a network of Desert Locust Control Centers, including establishing new centers and rehabilitating existing ones, investing in climate-proof and energy-efficient infrastructure, preparing a national control plan, and developing an integrated Desert Locust Early Response System to provide early warning and coordinate response

column7: Conduct public awareness campaigns on pesticide safety and climate-smart pest management
column12: Component 4 supports public awareness campaigns to inform communities about environmental and health effects of insecticides and promotes climate-smart pest management; campaigns will reach at least 75,000 beneficiaries and integrate COVID-19 preventive measures

column7: Share of affected pasture and agricultural land restored to productivity

column7: Affected households supported by social safety nets, with female recipients

column7: Development of locust control plan and functioning early warning system
column12: Outcome indicators include whether Yemen’s locust control plan is developed and whether an early warning system is developed and functioning

column7: Improve availability and access to food and nutritious diets and enhance capacity to respond to food insecurity

column7: Cash-for-work program to restore agricultural infrastructure and build climate resilience

column7: Distribute climate-smart input packages and provide training for crop, livestock and fish production
column12: Component 2 will increase production and sale of nutritious crop, livestock and fish products by restoring climate-smart local production systems through input packages (crop seeds, animal feed, forage seeds, fish production equipment, beekeeping kits and dairy equipment) and training (Farmer Field Schools, veterinary services), promoting climate-smart production

column7: Provide value addition packages and grants for processing and marketing of agri-food products
column12: Under Component 2, in-kind grants will support value addition through processing, packaging and marketing, including dairy, hydroponics and greenhouses, to promote commercialization of nutritious food products

column7: Supply horticulture kits and promote climate-smart vegetable production using greenhouses, drip irrigation and hydroponics
column12: Component 3 will improve nutritional status and incomes of vulnerable households by distributing horticulture production kits and feed for livestock, and by introducing innovative climate-smart vegetable production methods using greenhouses, drip irrigation and hydroponics, targeting vulnerable and women-headed households

column7: Strengthen extension services and animal health institutions, including training and laboratory upgrades
column12: Component 4 will build capacity for food security management by expanding extension services via farmer field schools, supporting animal health institutions through training of veterinarians, development of surveillance protocols, upgrading laboratories and establishing clinics, strengthening seed and plant health institutions with equipment and rehabilitation of seed quality control laboratories, and reinforcing apiculture institutions with training and equipment

column7: Improved household food access and dietary diversity
column12: PDO-level outcome indicators measure the percentage of households with improved Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES), the percentage of women with minimum dietary diversity, and the percentage of children consuming minimum acceptable diet

column7: Increased volume of agri-food products commercialized by beneficiaries
column12: PDO-level outcomes include an increase in the volume of agri-food products commercialized by beneficiaries, including female beneficiaries

column7: Improved preparedness to respond to food security crises
column12: Outcome 2 of the PDO-level indicators states that preparedness to respond to food security crises is improved through adoption of the food security preparedness plan and use of the Earth Observation monitoring tool

column7: Short-term results: jobs created and households receiving production packages

column7: Increase productivity and market access by selected producers, improve management of natural resources and provide crisis response
column12: The Project Development Objective is to increase the productivity and access to markets by selected producers, improve management of targeted productive natural resources, and provide immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency

column7: Strengthen national institutions for climate-smart agriculture and veterinary services

column7: Strengthen fisheries management and community-based fisheries plans
