column12: Subcomponent 2.2 establishes a matching grant program providing small and larger grants to farmers, fishers and producer organizations to adopt innovations and climate-smart technologies and to purchase post-harvest equipment, with emphasis on targeting women and youth

column12: Component 3 establishes an Agriculture Sector Coordination Division (ASCD) responsible for project management, monitoring and evaluation, fiduciary management and communications

column7: Increased productivity and improved market access for selected producers
column12: PDO-level results indicators include increased productivity (yields of crops and livestock) and improved market access measured by the value of sales

column12: The Project Development Objective is to address the early and medium-term resilient disaster recovery needs of cyclone-affected people

column7: Provide cash transfers, agricultural inputs and livestock restocking for immediate recovery
column12: Component 1 provides conditional and unconditional cash transfers for food, distribution of agricultural inputs and livestock restocking for affected households, and restoration of basic health services

column7: Rehabilitate critical community infrastructure and implement risk reduction measures
column12: Component 2 finances rehabilitation of critical community infrastructure—water supply, sanitation, irrigation schemes, schools, and roads—and risk reduction interventions such as slope protection and environmental rehabilitation

column7: Provide project management and technical assistance including community risk assessments and monitoring
column12: Component 3 includes project management and technical assistance, community risk assessments, displacement monitoring, health information and epidemic surveillance systems, and strategic communications

column7: People benefiting from cash transfers

column7: Households receiving agricultural inputs and livestock support
column12: PDO indicators include the number of households receiving agricultural and livestock support

column7: People benefiting from rehabilitated infrastructure and risk reduction interventions
column12: PDO indicators include the number of people benefiting from rehabilitated community infrastructure and risk reduction interventions

column7: Improve livestock productivity and access to market in selected regions
column12: The objective is to improve livestock productivity and access to market in selected regions

column12: Subcomponent 1.1 will update policies and legislation to address climate change, sustainable pasture management, animal welfare, monitoring greenhouse gas emissions and gene pool preservation, promoting repurposing public support and sustainable livestock development

column7: Strengthen veterinary services with information systems, modern facilities and staff training

column7: Enhance extension and advisory services with training and demonstration of climate-smart practices
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 strengthens public extension and advisory services by conducting capacity assessments, upgrading facilities, training staff through a training-of-trainers model, and demonstrating climate-smart practices such as improved feed and nutrition, breed improvement, animal health, manure management and renewable energy

column7: Upgrade public livestock research institutions for climate-smart technologies
column12: Subcomponent 1.4 strengthens public livestock research and development institutions by investing in infrastructure, equipment and training to develop climate-smart technologies including high-yielding drought-resistant forage crops, animal feed, nutrition and energy efficiency

column12: Subcomponent 2.1 establishes or modernizes livestock market infrastructure, such as market centers, slaughterhouses and milk collection centers, with energy-efficient and climate-resilient designs and provides capacity building and market information systems

column12: PDO indicators track increased participation of smallholder farmers in formal markets

column7: Expand seedling production using modern technology and partnerships
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 expands production of quality seedlings through modern technology, including partnerships with private sector nurseries and involving female-operated nurseries

column12: PDO-level indicators include the area of coastal forest under community-based management and the share of beneficiaries satisfied with project interventions

column12: The Agriculture Partnerships and Support component offers agribusiness partnership grants to commercial investors partnering with groups of smallholder farmers and provides an agriculture supplemental equity facility to support large agri-investments

column7: Provide program management, monitoring and capacity building for rural development
column12: The Program Management component finances management and monitoring of the program, including capacity building for community and government structures to support rural development

column7: Beneficiaries with improved access to rural infrastructure and services
column12: Key results indicators include the number of beneficiaries with improved access to rural infrastructure and services, disaggregated by gender

column7: Farming households engaged in productive partnerships
column12: Results indicators measure the number of farming households engaged in productive partnerships, including male and female households

column7: Increased volume of produce sold by households in agribusiness partnerships
column12: Results indicators include increased volume of produce sold by households engaged in agribusiness partnerships

column7: Beneficiaries receiving agriculture and livestock support to recover incomes after floods
column12: Results indicators measure the number of beneficiaries receiving agriculture and livestock support to recover incomes after floods

column7: Promote the development of MSMEs and value chain actors in agriculture, tourism and associated sectors
column12: "To promote the development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and relevant value chain actors in the agriculture, tourism and associated sectors in Comoros."

column7: Regulatory reform and extension services to support agriculture and tourism value chains
column12: The project will support regulatory reform to improve the investment climate, establish an agriculture data unit and extension programming using radio/SMS, create a one‑stop shop for business compliance and tourism institutional improvements such as investment promotion campaigns and community lodging initiatives.

column7: Upgrade rural economic development centers and provide climate‑smart agriculture training
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 finances upgrading rural economic development centers (CRDEs) with irrigation, seed storage, demonstration plots and tree nurseries and trains trainers and farmers on irrigation maintenance, improved seed multiplication and climate‑smart technologies.

column7: Provide poultry kits, veterinary training, artificial insemination and disease surveillance
column12: The project provides poultry breeding kits (kuroiler breed, feed and coops), scholarships and training for animal health assistants, national disease monitoring and surveillance, artificial insemination and vaccination campaigns against CBPP, Newcastle disease and FMD, and establishes dairy and poultry hubs offering inputs and aggregation services.

column7: Invest in cold storage, dry storage and rural road rehabilitation
column12: Subcomponent 1.3 invests in solar PV‑powered cold storage for poultry meat and eggs, dry storage/warehouses for fruits and vegetables, mechanical handling equipment at ports and rehabilitation of 36.9 km of rural roads to reduce travel time and improve market access.

column7: Business plan competition and matching grants for MSMEs and cooperatives
column12: Component 2 organizes a business plan competition that offers training, mentorship and grants to entrepreneurs and operates a matching grant fund that provides grants and capacity building to enterprises and cooperatives in agriculture and livestock value chains; subprojects may include multi‑purpose grinding/drying facilities, milk collection routes and other processing equipment.

column7: Increase in revenue of targeted MSMEs
column12: The results framework lists a PDO indicator of increased revenue among targeted micro, small and medium enterprises participating in the project.

column7: Increased volume of marketed agricultural products
column12: PDO indicators include an increase in the volume of agricultural products sold by project beneficiaries, reflecting higher productivity and market access.

column7: Jobs created through project‑supported enterprises
column12: PDO indicators measure the number of direct jobs created by project‑supported firms and cooperatives, including youth employment.

column7: Private finance catalyzed by the project
column12: The results framework tracks the value of private finance catalyzed through the project’s matching grants and business support mechanisms.

column7: Adoption of agricultural investment plans and tourism promotion actions
column12: Intermediate indicators include adoption of agriculture investment plans, establishment of an agriculture data unit, and implementation of tourism investment promotion campaigns, signalling institutional reforms and policy changes.

column7: Improved agricultural productivity and services
column12: Intermediate indicators track the number of multi‑service platforms and technicians trained, farmers benefiting from enhanced extension services, increases in yields of targeted commodities and the establishment of dairy hubs and cold storage facilities.

column7: Improved market infrastructure and cooperative development
column12: Indicators measure the number of cooperatives established and trained, the volume of milk aggregated, the number of cold storage facilities operational and kilometers of rural roads rehabilitated, reflecting improved market infrastructure and value chain efficiency.

column7: Women’s and youth participation in business support activities
column12: The project tracks the proportion of firms receiving grants that are owned or led by women and youth, as well as satisfaction ratings among beneficiaries and the resolution of grievances, aiming to enhance inclusion and empowerment.

column7: Improve integrated landscape management and promote climate‑smart productive practices in selected watersheds
column12: "Improve integrated landscape management and promote climate‑smart productive practices in selected watersheds"

column7: Develop Integrated Watershed Action Plans with regenerative livestock components and align incentives
column12: Component 1 will develop or improve Integrated Watershed Action Plans for at least ten watersheds, integrating regenerative livestock components using climate‑sensitive models, engaging stakeholders and aligning incentives and policy instruments through certifications and interinstitutional agreements.

column7: Coordinate public and private programs and leverage financing tools for landscape management
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 supports coordination of public and private programs to promote integrated landscape management, aligning policies and subsidies, engaging development banks like FIRA and leveraging the FOLUR Global Platform to mobilize financing and promote value chain sustainability.

column7: Provide technical assistance and business training to producer groups through local providers
column12: Component 2 strengthens business skills of producer groups by financing Local Providers of Technical Assistance to deliver advisory services and training on management, governance, financial literacy, marketing, land management, animal well‑being, veterinary services, value chain development and access to credit; specialized consultancies may cover market analysis, sustainable milk processing, cheese production, ecotourism services and credit access.

column7: Support climate‑smart ranching and agroforestry practices and restoration activities
column12: Component 3 finances subprojects for regenerative ranching and agroforestry systems, including living fences, pasture improvement, rotational grazing, tree planting, animal health and watering systems, training and experimental farms; it also supports agroforestry systems for shade coffee, cacao and pepper, and conservation practices such as voluntary conservation areas, fire prevention training, nurseries, reforestation and community monitoring of biodiversity and water quality.

column7: Strengthen stakeholder participation and knowledge management through learning platforms
column12: Component 4 enhances project coordination and knowledge management by creating a national learning community on regenerative ranching and agroforestry, establishing a virtual platform for sharing best practices and addressing gender and social inclusion, and supporting monitoring and evaluation and communications.

column7: Area of landscape under improved climate‑smart practices
column12: The PDO indicators include the number of hectares under improved climate‑smart agricultural practices, with a target of 450,000 ha.

column7: Farmers adopting improved agricultural technology
column12: PDO indicators measure the number of farmers adopting improved agricultural technology, with a target of 10,000 farmers (disaggregated by gender).

column7: Producer groups implementing climate‑smart practices that increase productivity
column12: A PDO indicator tracks the share of producer groups implementing climate‑smart practices that increase productivity by at least 10 percent, targeting 70 percent of participating groups.

column7: Inclusive landscape plans, policy instruments and restored land
column12: Intermediate indicators include the development of inclusive integrated landscape management plans, adoption of commodity value‑chain policies or certifications, producer groups with improved management capacities, restoration of 10,500 ha of land, watersheds with community monitoring systems, and satisfaction and grievance indicators.

column7: Strengthen governance and management of targeted fisheries and improve handling of landed catch at selected sites
column12: The development objective of this first phase of the West Africa Regional Fisheries Program is to strengthen governance and management of targeted fisheries and improve handling of landed catch at selected sites.

column7: Develop legal frameworks, vessel registration and rights‑based fisheries management
column12: Component 1 strengthens good governance and sustainable management of fisheries by developing legal and operational policies, strengthening vessel registration systems, introducing rights‑based fisheries management schemes and improving data collection and communication systems.

column7: Implement monitoring, control and surveillance systems to reduce IUU fishing
column12: Component 2 reduces illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing by providing monitoring, control and surveillance systems (MCS) and legal assistance to align national legislation with the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

column7: Invest in infrastructure and institutional capacity to improve fish handling and reduce post‑harvest losses
column12: Component 3 increases the contribution of fish resources to the local economy by investing in landing site infrastructure and institutional capacity to improve the handling of landed fish and reduce post‑harvest losses.

column7: Publication of fisheries management data
column12: PDO indicators include the share of fisheries management data that is publicly available, reflecting greater transparency and policy reform.

column7: Secure fishing rights allocated to small‑scale fishers
column12: PDO indicators measure the allocation of secure fishing rights in the small‑scale fisheries segment, supporting income stability and tenure security for artisanal fishers.

column7: Number of vessels operating within established ceilings and inspected for compliance
column12: The results framework tracks the number of fishing vessels operating within established capacity ceilings and the share of vessels inspected for compliance with regulations, contributing to sustainable fisheries management and conservation of marine resources.

column7: Improved handling and marketability of landed fish
column12: PDO indicators include the share of marketable fish landed at selected sites, reflecting improved handling practices and reduced post‑harvest losses.

column7: Direct project beneficiaries, including women
column12: The results framework counts the number of direct project beneficiaries, including the share of female beneficiaries, reflecting efforts to ensure inclusivity and women’s participation.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Improve access to productive assets, services and markets for pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists and strengthen capacity for crisis response
column12: "Improve access to essential productive assets, services and markets for pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists in selected trans‑border areas and along transhumance axes across six Sahel countries, and strengthen country capacities to respond promptly and effectively to pastoral crises or emergencies."

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Upgrade veterinary infrastructure, train animal health workforce and conduct mass vaccination campaigns
column12: Component 1 upgrades veterinary infrastructure (veterinary clinics, posts, border inspection posts and vaccination pens), provides training for animal health professionals and finances region‑wide vaccination campaigns and surveillance surveys targeting priority diseases such as CBPP and PPR.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Develop natural resource management plans and rehabilitate rangelands and water infrastructure
column12: Component 2 promotes natural resource management by negotiating and implementing management plans, marking transhumance tracks and rest areas, rehabilitating rangelands, creating pasture reserves, building and rehabilitating water facilities (wells, boreholes, ponds) and forming water‑user associations, while providing training and conflict resolution support.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Construct livestock markets, rural roads and processing units and support producer organizations
column12: Component 3 facilitates market access by constructing or rehabilitating 105 livestock markets, 300 km of rural roads and livestock rest areas, establishing small‑scale processing units such as milk collection centers and slaughter facilities and upgrading market information systems; it also builds capacity of producer organizations in governance, business management and trade facilitation.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Strengthen early warning systems and provide crisis response funding and livelihood diversification
column12: Component 4 enhances pastoral crisis management by strengthening early warning systems, developing response plans and establishing contingency funds; it also finances vocational training and micro‑projects to diversify livelihoods and provides rapid financing mechanisms to respond to emergencies.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Vaccination coverage for CBPP and PPR
column12: PDO‑level results indicators include vaccination coverage for contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and the number of small ruminants vaccinated against peste des petits ruminants (PPR), reflecting improved disease control and resilience of livestock systems.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Area under sustainable land management and improved water access
column12: Results indicators include the area under sustainable land management and reductions in distances between water points along transhumance routes, demonstrating improved natural resource management and ecosystem resilience.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Animals sold at rehabilitated markets and market efficiency
column12: PDO indicators track the number of animals sold at rehabilitated livestock markets, indicating improved market infrastructure and value chain efficiency.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Improved crisis response time for pastoral emergencies
column12: Results indicators include the response time to release funding for eligible emergencies, measuring the effectiveness of crisis response mechanisms.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Direct project beneficiaries and women’s participation
column12: PDO indicators report the number of direct project beneficiaries and the percentage of female beneficiaries, highlighting the project’s focus on inclusion and gender equity.

column7: Strengthen national and regional capacity for disease surveillance and provide effective emergency response
column12: "Strengthen national and regional cross‑sectoral capacity for collaborative disease surveillance and epidemic preparedness in West Africa, and provide immediate and effective response to eligible emergencies."

column7: Enhance surveillance and information systems with community and cross‑border coordination
column12: Component 1 enhances national surveillance and reporting systems, promotes cross‑border coordination and community engagement, and develops interoperable early‑warning systems and risk analysis tools to improve disease reporting and analysis.

column7: Strengthen veterinary and public health laboratory networks and accreditation
column12: Component 2 supports the establishment of networks of public health and veterinary laboratories, strengthens laboratory capacities for surveillance, pathology and diagnosis of priority diseases and antimicrobial resistance, improves data and specimen management and supports accreditation processes.

column7: Improve preparedness and emergency response through planning, rapid response teams and simulation exercises
column12: Component 3 enhances preparedness and emergency response capacity by supporting joint planning across sectors, expanding surge capacity through multidisciplinary rapid response teams, conducting simulation exercises and providing a contingent emergency response component for eligible emergencies.

column7: Strengthen human resource management and training for health surveillance and epidemic preparedness
column12: Component 4 strengthens government capacity for workforce planning and human resource management by leveraging training programs such as Field Epidemiology Training Programs (FETP) and veterinary FETP, addressing incentives for retention of skilled personnel and providing cross‑sectoral training for surveillance and preparedness.

column7: Improved capacity scores for surveillance reporting and laboratory testing
column12: The results framework measures progress toward International Health Regulations (IHR) and Joint External Evaluation (JEE) benchmarks, including the number of countries achieving higher scores for real‑time surveillance reporting, laboratory testing quality, zoonotic surveillance and emergency preparedness.

column7: Functional One Health platforms and cross‑border collaboration
column12: PDO indicators include establishment of a functional One Health platform for prioritizing zoonotic diseases and effective cross‑border collaboration and information sharing among participating countries.

column7: Strengthen cross‑sectoral disease surveillance capacity and provide emergency response
column12: "Strengthen national and regional cross‑sectoral capacity for collaborative disease surveillance and epidemic preparedness in West Africa, and provide immediate and effective response to eligible emergencies."

column7: Strengthen surveillance and information systems in participating countries
column12: Component 1 enhances national surveillance and reporting systems, improves cross‑border coordination, develops interoperable early warning systems and supports community‑level surveillance structures.

column7: Establish networks of public health and veterinary laboratories and improve specimen management
column12: Component 2 establishes networks of public health and veterinary laboratories, strengthens data and specimen management and links national laboratories to regional reference laboratories.

column7: Improve preparedness and emergency response, including contingency funding
column12: Component 3 improves outbreak preparedness and response capacity through joint planning and simulation exercises and provides contingent emergency response financing to address eligible emergencies.

column7: Train and retain human resources for disease surveillance and veterinary services
column12: Component 4 focuses on human resource management by supporting training programs (Field Epidemiology Training Program, Frontline and Applied Veterinary Epidemiology Training) and strategies to retain skilled health and veterinary workforce.

column7: Improved capacity scores for surveillance, laboratory quality and emergency preparedness
column12: The results framework uses International Health Regulations capacity scores to measure improvements in real‑time surveillance and reporting systems, laboratory quality, zoonotic disease surveillance, human resources and emergency preparedness in participating countries.

column7: Progress toward functional One Health platforms and cross‑sectoral collaboration
column12: PDO indicators assess progress toward functional One Health platforms and cross‑sectoral collaboration for disease surveillance, reflecting institutional reforms in veterinary and public health services.

column7: Strengthen disease surveillance capacity and provide emergency response (duplicate of REDISSE I)
column12: The PID for additional financing retains the REDISSE development objective to strengthen national and regional cross‑sectoral capacity for disease surveillance and provide emergency response.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Improve resilience of pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists in selected Sahel areas
column12: "Improve the resilience of pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists in selected areas in the Sahel region."

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Strengthen veterinary services, upgrade infrastructure and implement mass vaccination and surveillance
column12: Component 1 strengthens national veterinary services by upgrading clinics, posts, border inspection posts and vaccination pens; building human resource capacity through masters and doctorates; establishing digital disease information systems; updating strategic plans for PPR and CBPP; financing nationwide vaccination and surveillance campaigns; building laboratory capacity; and developing national action plans on veterinary medicines and antimicrobial resistance.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Establish community‑driven landscape management, restore rangelands and build water infrastructure
column12: Component 2 supports sustainable landscape management by creating community‑driven mechanisms, building capacity of decentralized land authorities, delineating transhumance tracks and rest areas, establishing local conflict management committees, restoring rangelands and promoting manure and nutrient management; it constructs and rehabilitates wells, boreholes and ponds and forms water‑user committees, and trains agro‑pastoral field schools on fodder production and improved feeding practices.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Develop strategic market infrastructure, build capacity of pastoral organizations and finance value‑chain subprojects
column12: Component 3 improves pastoral livestock value chains by rehabilitating or constructing small‑scale markets and rest areas along trade routes and digitizing market information systems (Subcomponent 3.1); conducting participatory assessments and action plans to strengthen national and regional pastoral producer organizations, including training on governance, business management, climate change and policy dialogue (Subcomponent 3.2); and financing subprojects that provide inputs, equipment and infrastructure for feed production, hide and skin processing, meat and milk processing, small‑ruminant fattening, and climate‑smart manure management (Subcomponent 3.3).

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Provide vocational training, social registry access and income‑generating grants for women and youth
column12: Component 4 enhances social and economic inclusion by financing vocational and technical training for vulnerable women and youth on climate‑smart agro‑pastoral practices, providing stipends and customized materials (Subcomponent 4.1); improving access to social and civil registries through diagnostic studies, technical assistance and civil registration campaigns (Subcomponent 4.2); and offering small grants (about US$450) and mentoring to women and youth for income‑generating activities such as fodder production and small‑scale processing of milk, hides and skins (Subcomponent 4.3).

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Coordinate project implementation, strengthen institutions and improve crisis preparedness
column12: Component 5 supports project coordination and monitoring by financing the PRAPS regional and national coordination units; strengthens institutional capacities through support for master’s and doctoral training, analytical studies using livestock investment and environmental assessment tools and training on climate adaptation; and enhances early warning systems, pastoral crisis preparedness, contingency planning and a contingent emergency response component.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Vaccination coverage for CBPP and number of small ruminants vaccinated for PPR
column12: PDO indicators include vaccination coverage rates for contagious bovine pleuropneumonia (CBPP) and the number of small ruminants vaccinated and marked against peste des petits ruminants (PPR) at regional and country levels.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Land area under sustainable landscape management
column12: The results framework measures the land area under sustainable landscape management practices in hectares for each country and regionally, reflecting improvements in ecosystem management.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Income increase among pastoral households
column12: A PDO indicator tracks the income increase of pastoral households generated with the support of the project, with targets disaggregated by country.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Implementation of national strategic plans for PPR and CBPP and improved veterinary infrastructure
column12: Intermediate indicators include the level of implementation of national strategic plans for PPR and CBPP, the number of veterinary units built or rehabilitated and functional and the number of vaccination pens built or rehabilitated, indicating institutional improvements in animal health services.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Inspections of veterinary medicines and establishment of regional veterinary committee
column12: Intermediate results indicators track the number of inspections dedicated to controlling veterinary medicines implemented through the project and the operationalization of a regional veterinary committee, contributing to improved regulation and animal health safety.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Functional committees for sustainable landscape management and access to water
column12: Indicators measure the number of functional committees for sustainable management of landscapes facilitating mobility and the number of functional water points accessible to (agro)pastoralists on mobility routes, demonstrating improved governance of natural resources and water availability.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Cultivated fodder production and agreements on peaceful transhumance
column12: Intermediate indicators include the quantity of cultivated fodder produced and available to pastoralists and the number of bilateral or multilateral agreements facilitating peaceful transhumance, contributing to improved feed availability and reduced conflict along mobility routes.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Reduction of conflicts linked to mobile livestock systems
column12: The results framework includes an indicator for the reduction rate of conflicts linked to mobile livestock systems along transhumance and trade axes, with targets increasing over the project period.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Operational markets along regional routes and implementation of action plans by producer organizations
column12: Indicators measure the number of operational livestock markets built or rehabilitated along regional trade routes and the implementation rate of action plans developed by umbrella pastoral organizations, reflecting enhanced market infrastructure and organizational capacity.

column3: Burkina Faso; Chad; Mali; Mauritania; Niger; Senegal
column7: Beneficiaries of innovative value‑chain subprojects
column12: An intermediate indicator counts the number of direct beneficiaries of innovative subprojects to valorize pastoral value chains, disaggregated by country, demonstrating outreach and impact of the value‑chain financing component.

column7: Improve resilience of pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists in selected areas (same as PRAPS‑2)
column12: The additional financing retains the PRAPS‑II development objective to improve the resilience of pastoralists and agro‑pastoralists in selected areas in the Sahel region.

column7: Scale up community‑based landscape restoration and fire management
column12: Under subcomponent 2.1, the additional financing scales up community‑based interventions to generate revenues and protect natural pastoral areas through building fire strips (1,000 km), constructing stone cordons (350 km), establishing pastoral reserves and assisting natural regeneration in Mauritania; in Niger it finances restoration of degraded land, dune fixation, fire strips, improved rangelands and removal of invasive species.

column7: Construct and rehabilitate climate‑resilient water infrastructure
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 finances the construction and rehabilitation of additional climate‑resilient water points, including boreholes, pastoral wells and watering ponds, in Mauritania and Niger, and establishes committees to manage, monitor and maintain these water facilities.

column7: Expand cultivated fodder and food crop production with climate‑smart practices
column12: Subcomponent 2.3 supports development of additional cultivated fodder sites (irrigated and rainfed), provision of drought‑tolerant seeds and small equipment, storage units and irrigation infrastructure, and technical assistance for climate‑smart fodder and food crop production; in Niger it includes small irrigation infrastructure, seed banks, rehabilitation of feed stores and training on improved livestock feeding practices.

column7: Provide cash grants for income‑generating activities to vulnerable pastoralists
column12: Under subcomponent 4.3, the additional financing provides cash grants of about US$450 per person to vulnerable pastoral and agro‑pastoral households in Niger to support income‑generating activities such as small processing units, sheltered mills, warehouses and storage facilities, thereby enhancing economic resilience.

column7: Increase regional collaboration and health system capacities to prevent, detect and respond to health emergencies
column12: "Increase regional collaboration and health system capacities to prevent, detect and respond to health emergencies in Western and Central Africa."

column7: Develop health security governance, NAPHS, cross‑border preparedness and compliance assessments
column12: Subcomponent 1.1 provides technical assistance to develop and monitor National Action Plans for Health Security, foster joint cross‑border outbreak preparedness and investigations, conduct operational and analytical research, assess compliance with International Health Regulations and Performance of Veterinary Services through JEEs and PVS evaluations and establish regional strategies and human resource plans.

column7: Operationalize One Health and combat antimicrobial resistance through surveillance and awareness
column12: Subcomponent 1.2 finances technical support to operationalize the One Health approach by establishing coordination platforms, developing guidelines and standard operating procedures, setting up real‑time One Health surveillance systems, monitoring implementation and conducting learning activities; it also funds development of regional AMR surveillance guidelines, education and awareness campaigns on AMR, research and behavioral interventions to promote responsible antibiotic use, and infection prevention and control measures.

column7: Enhance collaborative surveillance and digital platforms for health emergencies
column12: Subcomponent 2.1 supports collaborative surveillance by reviewing priority disease lists, developing a regional strategy, strengthening WAHO’s Health Information System unit, integrating One Health data using interoperable digital platforms, developing dashboards for scenario planning and real‑time surveillance, mapping human, livestock and wildlife surveillance systems, developing multi‑sectoral data protocols and platforms, supporting joint risk assessments and simulations and building machine‑learning platforms to analyse epidemiological data.

column7: Strengthen laboratory quality, biosafety and specimen management across the region
column12: Subcomponent 2.2 strengthens laboratory networks by supporting quality control, biosafety and biosecurity policies, establishment of laboratory information management systems, antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic disease diagnostic capacity, twinning programs between national reference laboratories and centres of excellence, biospecimen surveillance at the regional biobank and sample transportation protocols and quality management mentoring.

column7: Develop multi‑disciplinary health workforce and training programs
column12: Subcomponent 2.3 supports development and implementation of an ECOWAS public health workforce strategy, assessment and standardization of Field Epidemiology and Laboratory Training Programs and development of new expertise in disaster management, informatics, epidemic modelling and other technical areas through training and capacity building.

column7: Support health emergency management and rapid response teams
column12: Subcomponent 3.1 develops standardized training programs in public health emergency management and Good Emergency Management Practice, builds rosters of integrated regional rapid response teams, conducts simulation exercises, integrates gender‑transformative initiatives, establishes risk communication and community engagement systems, trains staff on biosafety, biosecurity, IPC, emergency management, genomic sequencing and climate change preparedness and strengthens regional mechanisms for mobilizing health professionals during emergencies.

column7: Improve health service delivery during emergencies and develop response guidelines
column12: Subcomponent 3.2 conducts regional assessments of infection prevention and control protocols, develops guidelines for continuity of health services during emergencies, builds capacity in clinical management and IPC, supports countries to develop disease outbreak response plans including stockpiling of medical commodities and conducts operations research on uptake and equity of response strategies.

column7: Support program management, coordination and advocacy
column12: Component 4 finances project implementation, including procurement, financial management, environmental and social management, monitoring and evaluation and staff training; it organizes regional steering committees and mobilizes technical and financial partners, conducts advocacy and awareness raising on risk communication and citizen engagement and provides technical assistance to participating countries.

column7: Cross‑border collaboration agreements and harmonized policies
column12: PDO‑level outcome indicators include the number of agreements signed for cross‑border collaboration and information sharing facilitated by WAHO and the number of regionally harmonized policies, strategy frameworks or protocols developed by ECOWAS to strengthen health security and systems resilience.

column7: Costed plans for veterinary services and One Health roadmaps developed and implemented
column12: PDO indicators measure the number of participating countries that have costed five‑year plans to address gaps in veterinary services’ critical competencies based on PVS Gap Analysis and the number of costed One Health roadmaps developed and implemented by national coordination mechanisms.

column7: People trained in health security and gender mainstreaming activities
column12: Intermediate results indicators track the number of people trained in field epidemiology, laboratory and health security short courses, including the percentage of women trained, and the number of regional gender mainstreaming activities and technical assistance events provided.

column7: Annual cross‑border health security collaboration activities and animal health training
column12: Intermediate indicators include the number of annual cross‑border health security collaboration activities organized and the number of people trained in animal health (with percentage of women), demonstrating enhanced preparedness and regional cooperation.

column7: PVS Pathway missions conducted and grievances addressed
column12: Intermediate results include the number of PVS Pathway missions conducted to strengthen veterinary services and the percentage of complaints or grievances addressed related to WAHO’s interventions.
